content: Manchester City captain Vincent Kompany argues that UEFA's Financial Fair Play (FFP) regulations protect established clubs rather than fostering competition. He believes these rules hinder smaller or less wealthy clubs from challenging the dominant teams. Kompany claims that City's recent successes and financial stability would not have been possible under FFP, which he sees as safeguarding the status quo and limiting opportunities for growth in other clubs.

Jeff Williams, a 26-year-old England Sevens international who has scored 36 tries on the World Series circuit, has signed with Bath for the upcoming season. Bath head coach Mike Ford is excited about Williams' addition, noting his dynamic playstyle and fit with the team's attacking approach, while also aligning with their policy of developing young English talent. Williams, whose background includes playing for clubs in South Africa and France, will transition from sevens to 15s rugby at Bath.

Director David Ayer revealed the first full look at Jared Leto playing the Joker in "Suicide Squad," a film set for release in 2016 without the presence of Batman. Leto has completely transformed for the role, cutting his hair and shaving his face, and he will be the first actor to portray the character since Heath Ledger. The movie, which also stars Will Smith and Margot Robbie among others, is scheduled to hit theaters on August 5, 2016.

Three Florida corrections officers and a former officer trainee have been charged with plotting to kill a former inmate, according to the Florida Attorney General's office. They infiltrated a KKK branch and were approached by an FBI informant about carrying out the killing, which they allegedly wanted revenge for a previous fight with the inmate. The FBI staged a fake crime scene to secure their confessions, and the men could face up to 30 years in jail if convicted.

The conference call for Manny Pacquiao and Floyd Mayweather Jr. regarding their upcoming fight was abruptly canceled due to technical difficulties caused by a high number of participants. Pacquiao managed to answer just one question before the call was cut short, to which he replied that his training was going well. The call was rescheduled, and Mayweather was set to have his own conference call the following day.

Serena Williams received a large cake to celebrate her 700th career victory at the Miami Open, following her victory over Sabine Lisicki. Meanwhile, Andy Murray also celebrated his 500th win with a cake. Despite the celebration, Williams faced a close match against Lisicki but ultimately progressed to the semi-finals, where she will play against Simona Halep.

Beijing International Airport is constructing the world's largest terminal, Terminal 1, to accommodate the dramatic rise in Chinese tourists traveling internationally. Designed by Zaha Hadid, this massive 700,000-square-meter facility aims to handle 45 million passengers annually and features a unique design that emphasizes open spaces and seamless user flow, reflecting Chinese culture and landscape. The new terminal exemplifies China's growing influence in global tourism, with outbound Chinese tourists increasing from 10 million in 2000 to 109 million by 2014, spending $164 billion.

Manchester United's manager, Louis van Gaal, reported that Wayne Rooney suffered a knee injury during Manchester United's loss to Everton, though the severity is still unknown. This defeat marked the first back-to-back losses under van Gaal's management and could potentially jeopardize United's position in the top four for Champions League qualification. Additionally, the injury occurred during a match where Rooney appeared in pain, further complicating matters for the team.

Manchester City is reportedly considering signing Jack Wilshere, who plays for Arsenal, but during his recent day off, Wilshere was seen sharing his extensive shopping trip on Instagram, which included items like cereal, eggs, and baked beans. Despite his upcoming return to play after a five-month absence due to ankle surgery, Wilshere humorously captioned his post about the effort needed to put away his groceries, asking for help from his followers to lift the heavy load.

A Venezuelan woman named Marleni Olivo threw a mango inscribed with her contact information at President Nicolas Maduro during a rally, an act that gained viral attention. In response, Maduro granted Olivo an apartment as part of his housing mission, addressing the issue she had raised. While Maduro's critics saw the incident as a potential political stunt, Olivo claimed her intention was simply to gain his attention to address her housing needs.

Carlos Tevez, a former striker for Manchester United and City, believes that scoring goals is more challenging in Serie A compared to the Premier League. He attributes this to the stronger defending in Italy and less effective midfields in the Premier League, where he previously scored 84 goals and won three titles. Tevez also suggests that his current Juventus team is more balanced and could potentially achieve similar success, including winning the Champions League, as the team he played with at Manchester United.

Jamie Carragher criticized Yaya Toure for allegedly ducking out of the way during a free-kick taken by Jason Puncheon, which secured Crystal Palace's victory and effectively ended Manchester City's hopes of salvaging a positive result. Carragher argued that Toure, as part of a large wall of defenders, should have made an effort to prevent the goal rather than avoid the ball. The incident contributed to Manchester City falling nine points behind leaders Chelsea in the Premier League standings.

A 50-year-old Australian man died in Bali after collapsing at a hotel restaurant, with initial indications suggesting a heart attack was the cause. The incident occurred in the popular tourist town of Kuta, where the man was reportedly on holiday. Authorities are awaiting the results of an autopsy to confirm the cause of death, and are working with the Australian Consulate to facilitate any necessary medical examinations.

Former Australian cricket captain and commentator Richie Benaud was honored with a private funeral service in Sydney, attended by close family, friends, and ex-players like Shane Warne and Ian Chappell. Benaud, who passed away at 84 from skin cancer complications, was remembered for his significant contributions to cricket both as a player and commentator, though his family honored his wish for a quiet and private service. The cricket community paid tribute to him through memorials and tributes across Australia, highlighting his influence and popularity among fans worldwide.

Isobel Attwood, a 16-year-old schoolgirl from Winchester, Hampshire, has been missing for two days and is believed to be with a man in his 20s in Southampton, according to friends' social media posts. Police are concerned for her welfare and believe she may be in either the Winchester or Southampton areas. Authorities are urging Isobel to contact them or return home, emphasizing that she will not face trouble if she comes forward.

If Manchester City fail to qualify for the Champions League this season, key players like Sergio Aguero, David Silva, Joe Hart, and Yaya Toure could lose out on a combined £12 million in bonuses. The team is currently in fourth place but faces stiff competition from Liverpool, with both needing to avoid finishing fifth to secure their Champions League spots. Manchester City's manager, Manuel Pellegrini, acknowledges that the team has underperformed recently and needs to improve, facing challenges in securing high-profile signings while their rivals, particularly Manchester United, continue to strengthen their roster.

Martin Skrtel, a Liverpool defender, has dismissed rumors suggesting he might leave the Premier League club for Wolfsburg or Napoli, stating that his future remains at Liverpool despite his contract expiring in 2016. His agent has confirmed that the only offer on the table is an extension to his contract, and there is no truth to reports of any German club's interest. Skrtel, who has made over 200 league appearances for Liverpool since joining in 2008, recently played in the team's FA Cup semi-final loss to Aston Villa.

Cheryl Rios, a female CEO from Texas, sparked controversy by stating on Facebook that women should not be president due to their "hormones" preventing them from starting wars. Rios, who supports equal rights for men and women, believes this is supported by biblical reasoning though she did not cite any specific verses. Her comments were met with widespread criticism on social media, with many labeling her as a misogynist and hypocrite.

Mario Mandzukic, despite suffering injuries in a physical Champions League match against Real Madrid, is expected to be fit for the return leg at the Bernabeu, according to Atletico Madrid's coach Diego Simeone. Simeone confirmed that Mandzukic participated in training sessions and is likely to play alongside Antoine Griezmann in the attacking line-up for the crucial second leg match. Simeone also praised Griezmann's recent form and adaptation to his new position in the team.

Chelsea's Jose Mourinho spent the week preparing his team to face Marouane Fellaini, only to learn from a hotel doorman that Fellaini was not playing due to being there to obtain tickets for Eden Hazard. This unexpected twist led Mourinho to confirm that it was actually Fellaini's twin brother, Mansour, who had been seen around the hotel, and he played in the match where Chelsea won 1-0. Despite the initial confusion, Chelsea managed to effectively counter Fellaini's threat through tactical arrangements, securing a victory and moving closer to the Premier League title.

Dawn Milosky, a 45-year-old woman from Beachwood, New Jersey, was involved in a severe accident where her car overturned and caught fire. She was found unconscious in her 2006 Toyota Solara convertible by responding police officers who quickly freed her; she required medical intervention including defibrillation and CPR before being airlifted to a hospital. Milosky faces charges including driving while intoxicated and reckless driving.

A farmer in eastern China has become famous for owning a six-legged goat, nicknamed the "spider goat" by internet users. Born to two normal goats, the unusual kid, which initially had six legs of similar length, now has four forelegs and two hind legs, with two of the forelegs becoming shorter and unable to touch the ground. The farmer, Xiao Qibin, plans to let the goat grow naturally without attempting to remove the extra legs.

West Ham United is considering signing Javier Hernández, the star striker for Real Madrid who recently scored a crucial Champions League goal, as part of their summer recruitment plan. Hernández, a 26-year-old who will return to Manchester United at the end of the season, is expected to be available for around £7 million due to his lack of playing time under Louis van Gaal. Alongside Hernández, West Ham is targeting young players such as Pedro Obiang, Moussa Konate, and Fabian Schar to strengthen their squad before their final season at Upton Park.

Stuart McCall, the manager of Rangers, has dismissed the idea of his future at the club being decided before the end of the season, emphasizing that while he has improved the team's performance and restored self-belief among players and fans, they have yet to achieve anything significant. McCall also confirmed that there have been no conversations regarding his contract beyond the current season. Additionally, Shane Ferguson, who was part of a controversial loan deal with Newcastle United, is expected to join Rangers next week, though McCall is cautious about Ferguson's immediate contribution due to a long-term knee injury.

Werder Bremen secured a narrow 1-0 victory over Hamburg SV in a crucial match, thanks to an 84th-minute penalty by Franco Di Santo, which kept Bremen's hopes for a Europa League spot alive. Despite new coach Bruno Labbadia's return to Hamburg, the match ended with Hamburg in last place, while Bremen moved up to seventh. With five matches remaining, Labbadia faces the challenge of preventing Hamburg, the only team never to have played in the second division, from experiencing relegation for the first time.

A two-year-old boy fell into a cheetah exhibit at the Cleveland Metroparks Zoo after slipping between a 10 to 12-foot gap in the railing, but was rescued by his parents before emergency services arrived. The child suffered only minor injuries and was in stable condition after being taken to the hospital. The zoo plans to press child endangerment charges against the parents who had dangled their child over the railing.

Russian TV channel TV Rain gave Hillary Clinton's campaign video an 18+ rating due to concerns it might violate Russia's anti-gay propaganda law. The video included a brief scene of a gay couple holding hands, prompting the channel to avoid potential legal issues. This decision reflects the uncertainty surrounding the interpretation of the law, which bans "propaganda of nontraditional sexual relations" around minors, and follows similar actions taken in response to previous controversial content.

Siem de Jong, a 26-year-old Newcastle United midfielder, made a comeback appearance for the Under 21s team, playing 45 minutes before being substituted at halftime, following a long recovery from a collapsed lung. Despite this, his performance was described as subdued, suggesting he may not be ready for the upcoming match against Tottenham. Additionally, the article mentions that another loan signing, Facundo Ferreyra, also came off the bench during the game, despite not having featured in the senior team due to injuries.

Chef Ally Lees of Alfie Bird's restaurant in Birmingham created a massive omelette weighing 12,000 calories and measuring three feet in circumference for an Easter promotion. The omelette, made from 150 eggs, requires at least five people to consume due to its enormous size and high protein content, which is 16 times the recommended daily amount for a man. Chef Ally successfully prepared the record-breaking omelette in a specially used large paella pan, taking about an hour to cook thoroughly.

Three Olympic gold medalists from the 2012 London Olympics, Jessica Ennis-Hill, Mo Farah, and Greg Rutherford, will compete in the Sainsbury’s Anniversary Games at the Olympic Stadium. The event, which features a two-day Diamond League meeting and IPC Athletics Grand Prix, is set to take place from July 24-26 and aims to recreate the excitement of the 2012 games. Ticket sales have begun, with prices ranging from £10 to £20.

In Rio de Janeiro, a popular snack bar was found to be using the meat of stray dogs, killed with blows to the head, to make pastels, a traditional Brazilian pastry. The owner, Chinese Van Ruilonc, admitted to using the dogs, claiming they were strays collected from the streets. This discovery came alongside the investigation of alleged slave-like conditions for Chinese workers at the establishment, revealing a cage where workers were confined and forced to labor 18 hours a day without pay.

Ebony Dickens, using a pseudonym on Facebook, posted a threat to shoot every white cop she sees, which led to her arrest by local, state, and federal law enforcement agencies. The controversial post, detailing plans to kill multiple police officers, prompted a thorough investigation and resulted in the seizure of a firearm and multiple computers from Dickens' home during a subsequent search. Dickens was charged with disseminating information related to terrorist acts and released on a $10,000 bond after appearing in court.

PSV Eindhoven won the Dutch Eredivisie championship for the first time in seven seasons by defeating Heerenveen 4-1, securing 79 points and leaving Ajax Amsterdam behind in second place. Key to PSV's victory were two headed goals from Luuk de Jong and a stunning free-kick from Memphis Depay. Meanwhile, Dordrecht's loss to Vitesse Arnhem brought them closer to potential relegation, while AZ Alkmaar secured a spot in the Europa League playoffs with a 3-1 win over ADO Den Haag.

An 11-year-old boy named Shiva was reportedly beaten to death by his head teacher, Lalit Verma, at Dwarika Prasad School in Railamau village, India, after being accused of stealing another student's pencil and eraser. The severe beating led to Shiva's immediate death upon arrival at the hospital due to internal bleeding. This incident, among others, highlights the controversial use of corporal punishment by teachers in India, resulting in multiple reports of young boys dying under similar circumstances.

A gastrointestinal illness affecting 100 passengers and five crew members has broken out on the Celebrity Infinity cruise ship, which is currently 2,117 passengers strong. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) is investigating the cause of the illnesses but has not yet determined a specific origin. In response, the ship's operators have increased cleaning efforts and are cooperating with CDC testing.

Loren Mathieson captured a unique video of her Boston Terrier, Gizmo, performing an impressive "paw-stand" walking trick after trying on new booties. The footage shows Gizmo taking a few steps, then lifting his hind legs off the ground to walk in a vertical position before reaching Mathieson on the floor. The amusing clip has gained over 80,000 views and left many viewers smiling.

New Orleans has implemented a city-wide smoking ban, which took effect on Wednesday at midnight, prohibiting smoking in most venues such as bars, casinos, and restaurants. Despite some concerns from bar owners about potential revenue loss and objections from smokers, the ban was passed unanimously by the city council in January. However, a lawsuit challenging the ban is pending in state court, with a hearing scheduled in a month, and fines for violations start at $50.

Manchester United secured a crucial victory over West Ham United in the Under 21 Premier League, moving four points clear at the top of the table. Despite taking an early lead through Josh Cullen's header, West Ham equalized within 12 minutes only for Manchester United to quickly regain the upper hand with goals from Josh Harrop and Joe Rothwell. Adnan Januzaj, who captained the team, added to the win late in the game, ensuring a comfortable victory for Manchester United.

The Archbishop of Brisbane, Phillip Aspinall, has joined a local Catholic priest in advocating for the removal of Queensland's 'gay panic' homicide defense from the state's common law. This legal defense can reduce murder charges to manslaughter if a defendant claims they felt threatened by a sexual advance. In supporting this call, Aspinall emphasized that violence is never a justifiable response to sexual advances or other forms of perceived threat.

Sandra Bullock has been named the world's most beautiful woman by People magazine for 2015, marking her as the oldest woman to receive this honor. In an interview, Bullock downplayed the accolade, emphasizing character traits such as being a good person and mother over physical appearance, and noted that she finds the most beauty in those who are not striving for perfection. The cover story also highlights her family life and efforts to maintain health and fitness beyond her 40s.

An improvised bomb explosion near a U.N. vehicle in Garowe, Somalia, killed six people, including four UNICEF aid workers, according to the United Nations Assistance Mission in Somalia. The attack, claimed by the terrorist group Al-Shabaab, occurred as the vehicle was transporting workers from their guest house to their office. In response, Somalia’s President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud condemned the attack as an assault on the country's future, particularly targeting UNICEF workers who were working to improve the lives of Somali children.

Gary Saurage, a wildlife park owner in Beaumont, Texas, was called to capture a 400-pound, 11-foot-long alligator from a family's backyard pond using only his bare hands. The alligator, which proved to be particularly aggressive, was successfully removed and taken to Saurage’s park. This incident highlights the ongoing issue of alligators in residential areas and reinforces Saurage’s advice to maintain a safe distance and avoid feeding these animals.

In eastern Turkey, five members of the Kurdistan Workers' Party (PKK) were killed and one injured in a clash with Turkish forces, while four Turkish soldiers were also wounded. Turkish officials, including Prime Minister Ahmet Davutoglu and President Recep Tayyip Erdogan, condemned the attack and vowed a strong response. This conflict, which has lasted over three decades and claimed an estimated 40,000 lives, stems from the Kurdish minority's fight for independence or the PKK's guerrilla campaign against the Turkish state.

Two 18-month-old twin boys tragically died after accidentally falling into a canal in Yuma, Arizona, on Friday morning. The boys were found in the water nearly two hours after the incident by a Border Patrol helicopter, and despite resuscitation efforts, they were pronounced dead upon arrival at the hospital. The area around the canal is commonly used by families and joggers, but the exact sequence of events leading to the boys' fall remains unclear.

Orlando City, a Major League Soccer team coached by Adrian Heath, has shown interest in signing Javier Hernández, the Mexican international forward who has struggled during his loan at Real Madrid. Despite eight European clubs also showing interest, including Manchester United, who are willing to sell Hernández for around £8 million, Orlando City stands out due to its strong Latin-American fanbase and previous discussions about a potential deal. Meanwhile, another young player, Andreas Pereira, whose contract Manchester United wants to revise, has attracted attention from several European clubs like Paris Saint-Germain and Juventus, after he rejected their initial offer.

Joel Burger, 24, proposed to his girlfriend Ashley King, also 23, setting the stage for a Burger King-themed wedding. The couple, who have known each other since kindergarten and nicknamed themselves after the fast-food chain, plan to serve drinks in personalized Burger King cups for their guests. They took their engagement photos outside their local Burger King and hope to hold the wedding there as well, despite needing permission from the international restaurant chain.

A secret police intelligence report from 1964 revealed that a hit band from the 1960s, along with notorious BBC DJ Jimmy Savile, frequented a notorious pedophile brothel in Battersea, South West London. This information emerged as part of an investigation into the property, which was known to be used by pedophiles. Detective Superintendent David Grey began looking into the brothel in 2013 after a woman came forward in 2003 to report that Savile had abused her in the 1970s.

Sadie, a German Shepherd from Alberta, Canada, has been captured on film using her nose to turn on an electric organ and sit down to play piano sonatas. Despite the minimalist and off-key nature of her performance, which includes a brief moment of self-doubt, Sadie continues to entertain her audience with her musical endeavors. The video of Sadie playing the piano has garnered over 12,000 views and has received positive feedback from viewers who find her performance cute and impressive.

A phone thief named Ivan Balashov took a selfie in a Russian shop while trying to steal a smartphone, but was caught when police recognized him from the picture. After selecting a phone he liked, Balashov attempted to steal it but was stopped by shop security and later fled with the phone. The police identified him based on the selfie and found out he had sold the stolen phone shortly after. Balashov was sentenced to a three-month suspended prison term.

A new documentary trailer for Amy Winehouse's life and music has been released, set for UK release on July 3rd. The film, titled "Amy: The Girl Behind the Name," aims to capture both the artist and the personal aspects of Winehouse's life, including her struggles with fame and substance abuse. The documentary includes extensive, previously unseen footage and unheard tracks, and has been endorsed by Winehouse's family.

The article suggests watching "The Big Bang Theory" on Thursday for an episode featuring the return of Christine Baranski and Laurie Metcalf as the show's characters' mothers. It also recommends tuning in to "Saturday Night Live" hosted by Scarlett Johansson on Saturday, and "Mom" on Thursday for its Emmy-worthy performances, particularly in the season finale. Additionally, the article highlights other shows like "Backstrom," "Blue Bloods," and "Younger," suggesting these for viewers interested in different genres and plotlines.

The hit British show Downton Abbey, which will conclude its run later this year, might see some of its beloved characters return in a new American adaptation titled "The Gilded Age." Created by Downton Abbey's original writer, Julian Fellowes, the new series will be set in 19th-century New York and features characters like the Dowager Countess Violet and the Earl and Countess of Grantham, portrayed by Dame Maggie Smith and Elizabeth McGovern respectively, in their younger versions. NBC is optimistic about the project and hopes to bring it to air as early as September.

Steven Gerrard is set to start for Liverpool in their FA Cup semi-final against Aston Villa at Wembley, marking what could be his final game at the national stadium before joining LA Galaxy. Manager Brendan Rodgers has selected Gerrard despite using him sparingly this season, praising his importance in big matches. Gerrard, who served a three-match ban, hopes to end his illustrious career with a trophy, following his last appearance at Wembley in 2012 for the League Cup.

A new Dr. Seuss book, "What Pet Should I Get?", has generated significant interest, leading to an increased first printing from 500,000 to 1 million copies to meet demand. This release marks the first original Dr. Seuss book since 1990 and features characters from his classic "One Fish Two Fish Red Fish Blue Fish." The book, which was discovered among the late Ted Geisel's (Dr. Seuss) belongings, is set to debut on July 28th, rekindling excitement for the beloved author's work.

Jessica Carey traveled over three hours to surprise her grandmother, Patty Lawing, with a tattoo of her from childhood on her forearm. The heartfelt gesture, captured on video, deeply moved Patty who reacted with emotion upon seeing the strikingly accurate depiction of herself as a young woman. Jessica, along with her husband and two children, planned the surprise visit and tattoo to make the moment memorable for Patty.

At 65 years old, Annegret Raunigk, a German primary school teacher, is set to give birth to quadruplets, making her the oldest known woman to carry and deliver such a high number of babies. This pregnancy, conceived through 18 months of fertility treatment, follows previous headlines about her giving birth to her youngest daughter at age 55. While her gynecologist notes the high-risk nature of the pregnancy due to her age, everything remains on track as of now.

Japan's space agency, JAXA, plans to send an unmanned rover to the moon by 2018, aiming to develop soft-landing technologies potentially applicable to future manned missions to the moon or Mars. This mission, which could cost between $83.4 million and $125 million, involves using the agency's Epsilon rocket to deploy the SLIM probe equipped with advanced face recognition software to identify landing sites. The move reflects Japan's efforts to catch up with its Asian rivals, such as China and India, which have achieved significant milestones in space exploration.

Brazilian football clubs are on high alert due to a dengue fever outbreak, with three players from Corinthians, including star striker Paolo Guerrero, diagnosed with the disease. The players are using insect repellent during practices and clubs are taking steps to eliminate potential mosquito breeding sites. The increase in dengue fever cases in Brazil this year has raised concerns among players, particularly as the disease can cause significant discomfort and requires several weeks to recover from.

Manchester United striker James Wilson, in an interview, expressed his admiration for Wayne Rooney's free-kick-taking ability, Robin van Persie's movement, and Radamel Falcao's instincts in the penalty box. Wilson, who has scored one Premier League goal this season, aims to learn from these experienced forwards to improve his game, having played alongside them in the Under 21 team. Wilson sees Rooney's consistent practice, van Persie's ability to create space, and Falcao's predatory instincts as qualities that could significantly enhance his own performance.

In Milwaukee, Wisconsin, Archie Brown Jr., who struck and killed a 2-year-old child with his van, was subsequently shot and killed at the scene by an unknown assailant, potentially in revenge. Additionally, a 15-year-old boy was also shot and later died, though his connection to the incident is unclear. The case remains under investigation by the police, who have not yet made any arrests.

A child from Memphis, Tennessee, has gained over 3,000 Twitter followers by posting pictures of himself in gang-related activities, including posing with guns and drugs, and using sexually explicit language. His tweets have sparked criticism from the public and authorities, who are concerned about the potential long-term impact on the child. Despite the backlash, the child has defended his actions, citing personal hardships and suggesting that the criticism affects his family.

John Schumann, former frontman of Redgum, expressed disappointment after his song "I Was Only 19" was used at Reclaim Australia rallies aimed at opposing Islamic law in Australia. The song, intended to promote compassion and inclusiveness, was co-opted by a "confused 'patriotic' movement," according to Schumann. Violence erupted at these rallies, leading to multiple arrests and minor injuries, with the federal Opposition Leader calling for an end to such violent expressions of free speech.

Emmanuel Adebayor, a forward for Tottenham, has dismissed rumors of a potential transfer and reaffirmed his commitment to staying at White Hart Lane. Despite facing competition from rising star Harry Kane, Adebayor, who joined the club in 2011, maintains he will continue to fight for a place in the team. His form has notably declined since his initial success, with only two goals scored this season across 16 appearances.

Stuart Pearce advocates for maintaining Manuel Pellegrini as Manchester City's manager despite the team's recent struggles. Pearce believes that the club should not rush into changing managers and instead focus on improving the squad during the summer transfer window. He attributes part of the team's poor performance to the declining influence of key player Yaya Toure.

Steve Bruce remains optimistic about keeping Hull City in the Barclays Premier League despite their recent 2-0 defeat to Southampton, which left them struggling to avoid relegation. Bruce attributes their difficulties to several long-term injuries to key players and believes that securing nine or eight more wins could secure their place in the league. Despite challenging upcoming fixtures against stronger teams like Liverpool and Arsenal, Bruce insists that his team is up for the challenge and confident in their ability to survive.

In Reading, a full-scale terror alert was triggered when a passer-by reported a suspicious object on a barge sailing down the Thames, which appeared to be a guided missile launcher with a dummy in a balaclava nearby. Upon investigation by Thames Valley Police and an Army bomb disposal team, the "weapon" was confirmed to be a non-threatening, purely ornamental dummy and a fake missile. Local residents criticized the prank as unnecessary and potentially dangerous given the current security climate.

Tiger Woods suffered an unusual injury during his play at the Masters when his club struck a tree root on the ninth hole, causing him to yelp in pain. Although he managed to continue playing and finished the tournament at 5-under-par, Woods reported that he had popped a ligament in his right wrist, which he was able to reposition to continue playing. Despite his injury, Woods tied for 17th place overall, marking his best finish in over a year at the Masters.

Iker Casillas, who has dedicated his entire career to Real Madrid, maintains his commitment to staying with the club despite potential competition from Manchester United's David de Gea. Casillas, now 33, expresses his willingness to fight for the starting goalkeeper position and fulfill his contract. He focuses on helping Real Madrid defend their Champions League title, acknowledging the tough upcoming matches against strong opponents.

A video has surfaced showing a failed missile launch of an S300 rocket in Russia, where the rocket barely managed to lift off before falling back to the ground, causing a small explosion and debris. This embarrassing incident occurred shortly after another rocket launch near Donetsk, Ukraine, resulted in the deaths of six Russian missile technicians and was only recently revealed to the public. These incidents reflect poorly on the Russian defense budget, which has increased by 33% over the past year under President Vladimir Putin's leadership.

Lancashire County Cricket Club has signed Australian all-rounder James Faulkner as their overseas player for much of this summer, replacing Peter Siddle. Faulkner, who recently won the World Cup with Australia, will join the team after completing his commitments in the Indian Premier League. The club's head coach, Ashley Giles, expressed excitement about Faulkner's arrival, praising his world-class status and potential to enhance the team's performance across all formats of the game.

In 1996, Mary Kay Letourneau, a 34-year-old teacher, had an affair with her 13-year-old student, leading to her imprisonment and the birth of a child with him. After serving over seven years, she was released in 2005 and married her former lover, Vili Fualaau, celebrating their 10th wedding anniversary in 2015. In an upcoming interview with ABC's "20/20," the couple will discuss how their marriage has endured despite the significant age gap and past challenges, including her status as a registered sex offender and his struggles with alcoholism and depression.

Jamie Carragher traveled to Spain during the international break to watch his son James play in the Under 12s group of the Mediterranean International Cup, a prestigious youth tournament held in Girona that attracts teams from over 36 countries. During his visit, Carragher even spoke to a local TV station and shared photos from the event on his Instagram account, where the Liverpool team drew 1-1 against a local Catalan side. The tournament, now in its 15th year, has featured many renowned players such as Lionel Messi and Neymar when they were younger.

Seattle-based filmmaker Gabriel Ng spent three months in Thailand, creating a stunning six-minute video that showcases the country's natural beauty and cultural sites using a drone-mounted camera. Filmed primarily on the island of Ko Samui, the video captures breathtaking coastal vistas, religious landmarks, and scenes of daily life, earning praise for its high-definition quality and capturing the essence of Thai tourism. This project follows previous work by Ng using drones for aerial filming, including weddings and famous U.S. locations.

Peter Moores, the current England coach, insists he can work with Michael Vaughan if he becomes the new director of cricket, despite their past disagreements. Moores believes the key is to ensure the best approach for improving the team, rather than adding another voice in the dressing room. Despite the upcoming changes in leadership, Moores remains focused on his role and is optimistic about the future, particularly with the emergence of promising young players.

Nottingham Forest intends to pursue a transfer for Blackburn's striker Jordan Rhodes, valued at £10 million, with the hope that a direct cash offer will succeed where previous attempts failed. Blackburn manager Gary Bowyer anticipates further interest in Rhodes' strike partner, Rudy Gestede, after Gestede scored 19 goals, including one against Forest. Several clubs, including Hull, Crystal Palace, West Brom, and Southampton, have shown interest in Gestede.

In a heartwarming scene captured in North Carolina, three dogs—a Husky named Sky and two Springer Spaniels named Sadie and Marshall—formed a unique musical ensemble by barking and howling in harmony. Starting with Sadie's bark, followed by Sky's melodious howl and Sadie's mimicry, the trio eventually harmonized, creating a surprisingly musical performance despite the unconventional instrument. The dogs continued their performance until their owner called for them to stop, leaving them looking surprised and disappointed.

The "French Spiderman," Alain Robert, climbed the 1,007-foot Cayan Tower in Dubai without a safety harness, using only sticky tape and chalk for assistance, taking an hour and a half to reach the top. This daring feat, captured on video, showcases Robert's exceptional skill and bravery, though it comes after a history of falls and legal issues during his previous climbs. Known as the "French Spiderman," Robert has previously climbed other tall structures around the world, including the Burj Khalifa, but always had to comply with local regulations.

An experimental cancer drug previously discarded due to poor results has shown promise in reversing the effects of Alzheimer's disease in mice, according to researchers at Yale University. The drug, AZD05030, works by blocking a process that damages nerve connections in the brain responsible for memory storage. Following these findings, human trials have been initiated to assess its effectiveness in Alzheimer's patients.

Marvel Studios has revealed the appearance of the Vision, played by Paul Bettany, in the upcoming "Avengers: Age of Ultron" sequel, putting an end to months of speculation. As part of the superhero trend, Netflix also released the real version of Charlie Cox's Daredevil suit for their new series. Additionally, the casting of Ben Hardy as the character Angel was announced for the upcoming "X-Men: Apocalypse" film, along with other updates on upcoming superhero movies.

Veteran referee Kenny Bayless has been chosen to officiate the highly anticipated fight between Floyd Mayweather and Manny Pacquiao, a decision that has raised some concerns due to Bayless's past favoritism towards Mayweather. Oscar De La Hoya, a former opponent of Mayweather who lost to him in 2007, believes Bayless's involvement gives an unfair advantage to Mayweather. Despite this, Bayless, known for his expertise and fairness, will be compensated generously for his role in the historic event.

Harry Kane's participation in the upcoming Under 21 European Championship is uncertain due to Tottenham Hotspur's scheduled post-season friendly in Malaysia. Manager Mauricio Pochettino is concerned about potential burnout for the 21-year-old striker, while the Football Association is in discussions with Tottenham regarding Kane's availability for the tournament. Kane, who recently made his England debut, has been told he will not be required for the senior team's upcoming matches against Ireland and Slovenia.

A measles outbreak affecting over 130 Californians due to a B3 strain has been declared over by the California Department of Public Health after 42 days without new cases. The majority of those affected (70%) were found to be unvaccinated, and the outbreak originated from visitors to Disney theme parks in December. Public health measures such as rapid case investigations, vaccinations, and heightened awareness effectively controlled the outbreak.

In San Miguel de Tucuman, Argentina, police are searching for a family of six who were photographed riding on a single motorbike without helmets, with two adults and four children aboard. This incident follows a similar case in Junin where a family of seven was spotted on the same mode of transport, both drawing widespread condemnation from social media users who found the behavior extremely dangerous. Authorities have appealed to the public for any information leading to the identification of these families.

A 44-year-old woman named Andrea McVeigh was severely injured when she was struck by a cyclist while walking on the pavement in Bermondsey, London. The cyclist fled the scene, prompting the woman’s husband to chase him. The incident left McVeigh scarred for life with multiple facial and hand injuries. Police have released CCTV footage of the cyclist and are appealing for the public's help in identifying him.

A headstone marking the burial site of Hillary Clinton's father, Hugh Rodham, was found tipped over in a cemetery in Scranton, Pennsylvania, just days after Clinton announced her candidacy for the presidency. The incident has sparked speculation and investigation; while police suspect vandalism, they are also considering weather-related causes. Local caretaker Paul McGloin, who has maintained the grave site since 1993, believes the timing of the incident is significant and coincidental with Clinton's announcement.

A California woman, Beatriz Paez, was recording police activity when a U.S. marshal took her phone, smashed it with his foot, and kicked it away, according to a video recorded by another witness. Paez, who felt her safety was compromised, plans to file a complaint and potentially a lawsuit against the marshals' actions. The U.S. Marshals Service is reviewing the incident, while Representative Janice Hahn has requested a federal investigation, arguing that Paez's rights were violated as she was not obstructing an investigation or arrest.

Max, a 18.5-inch tall corgi-Siberian husky cross, was found as a stray and has taken refuge at the Dogs Trust in Basildon, Essex. Despite his unusual appearance, Max is described as gentle, intelligent, and big-hearted and has become a favorite among the staff there. The increasing popularity of wolf-like dog breeds, influenced by TV shows like Game of Thrones, has led to an uptick in abandoned pets due to owners underestimating the care required for these breeds.

Chilean pickpockets have emerged as the most effective thieves in central London, according to undercover police reports, specializing in targeting wealthy tourists in areas like the West End. In one notable case, police intercepted two Chilean women in burkas who were found to be carrying €130,000, £20,000, and valuable jewelry. These organized gangs, which also include pickpockets from Romania, Algeria, and Bulgaria, operate in teams and use deceptive tactics to blend in with tourists.

In a severe car crash near Southam, Warwickshire, a young driver survived a rollover and became trapped under his vehicle. Despite suffering head, chest, and leg injuries, the man remained conscious throughout the rescue operation, which took 25 minutes by firefighters using specialized cutting tools. Emergency services praised the quick response of a community paramedic who began treatment immediately upon arrival.

Fly-tippers have dumped an unprecedented 40 tonnes of industrial waste along the side of the road in the Suffolk village of Walsham-le-Willows, shocking local authorities and residents alike. Described as the worst case of flytipping in a police officer's 28-year career, the dumped waste, including materials from the carpet and veterinary industries, will require significant resources to remove. Authorities are working to identify the perpetrators and are urging the public to report any suspicious activities related to flytipping.

A man who refused to comply with security staff at Toronto's Pearson International Airport was tasered and brought to the ground, after he attempted to enter a restricted area despite being told he could not board a flight. The incident, captured on video by a bystander, shows the man mumbling and holding onto a black briefcase as he was tasered, with a loud cry of pain audible immediately after the taser was deployed. The individual, believed to be in his 20s and possibly mentally disturbed, was later transferred to a hospital and held under Canada's Mental Health Act, with no criminal charges expected to be filed.

Serbia's President Tomislav Nikolic's government jet had to return to Belgrade after the co-pilot accidentally spilled coffee on the instrument panel, causing the plane to lose control and begin tumbling. The pilot managed to regain control and land safely, though the incident led to the cancellation of the president's planned meeting with Pope Francis. The co-pilot had his license suspended and admitted to activating the emergency slat button by mistake while trying to clean the coffee spill.

In South Africa, over 300 suspects have been arrested in connection with violent attacks against foreigners, which have forced thousands to seek refuge in temporary shelters. The government condemned these attacks and praised law enforcement for preventing further violence in cities like Durban. Despite the xenophobia, there has been an outpouring of support from South Africans who reject such actions and remind others of the country's history of relying on African neighbors for support during challenging times.

A skier named Zach Birnie captured harrowing footage of himself becoming caught in an avalanche while skiing off-piste in Revelstoke, Canada. Despite the heavy snow closing in around him and pushing him down the mountain, Birnie managed to emerge, though panting and shocked. Experts suggest that the fresh snow and steep terrain likely contributed to the avalanche, and recommend escaping the avalanche area, letting go of ski poles, opening bindings if possible, pulling knees to the chest, and holding arms in front of the face.

On the hottest day of the year, two men in their 20s stripped off their shirts before attempting to rob an Esso petrol station in Surrey, prompting a police investigation. The men, seen on CCTV, forcibly entered the manager's office but were interrupted by staff, leading to their escape without obtaining any cash. Surrey Police has released the images of the suspects and is urging the public for assistance in identifying them.

The Lada Niva 4x4, starting at £13,395 on the road, is gaining popularity despite its Soviet-era origins, thanks to its robust design and affordability compared to luxury alternatives like the Land Rover Defender. Despite being a no-frills vehicle with a simple plastic interior, the Niva's rugged capabilities make it a practical choice for off-road driving, and it's even available in a compact van format for £10,590. Interestingly, former Russian President Vladimir Putin reportedly used a Niva with a German engine in 2009, highlighting the car's durability and adaptability.

A lawsuit has been filed against the nation's largest provider of HIV and AIDS medical care, the AIDS Healthcare Foundation, accusing it of a $20 million scam involving kickbacks to boost funding from Medicare and Medicaid across 12 states. The former managers allege that employees and patients received kickbacks for patient referrals, with some employees earning $100 bonuses for referring positive test results. Despite the president of the foundation denying any wrongdoing, the lawsuit claims that the scheme originated in California and expanded to other locations.

Liz, a bearded dragon owned by Shannen Hussein, has been caught on video responding to her owner's question about hunger by nodding her head, demonstrating what appears to be an understanding of the English language. Following this interaction, Liz was rewarded with a superworm treat, which she enjoys greatly. Shannen's hobby farm also features other animal stars like her pet lamb Winter, who has gained internet fame through various Vine videos showcasing its playful antics.

A young man named Travis Hatfield from West Virginia became an internet sensation after posting a video of himself singing a George Jones song to his uncle, Jamie Joe Cline, who has Down syndrome. The video, which shows the two singing together weekly, has garnered over 410,000 views and showcases their musical bond. Inspired by his uncle's love for music, Travis dreams of pursuing a career in country music and hopes to secure a record deal in Nashville.

Nik Wallenda, the daredevil from the 'Flying Wallenda' family, plans to walk untethered on a 400-foot observation wheel in Orlando, Florida, on April 29, as it moves. The Orlando Eye, scheduled to open to the public on May 4, will offer views of central Florida from its air-conditioned capsules. This stunt sets apart from previous ones due to the larger scale of the wheel and the absence of a safety pole, though Wallenda is unlikely to complete a full rotation.

Medhi Benatia, a central defender for Bayern Munich, may miss both legs of the Champions League quarter-final against Porto due to a muscle injury, potentially for two to four weeks. This adds to Bayern Munich's already lengthy injury list, which includes several key players. Despite the setback, Bayern Munich remains a strong contender for multiple titles, including the Bundesliga championship and other competitions.

Bayern Munich defeated Porto 6-1 in the Champions League quarter-final second leg, advancing to the semi-finals under the guidance of Pep Guardiola. This victory adds to Bayern's impressive season with a total of 115 goals scored so far, and they are on track to potentially score up to 141 goals if they maintain their current pace. Despite their dominant performance, the pressure is on the rest of Europe to match Bayern's exceptional level of scoring.

Fernando Torres credits Diego Simeone as the key figure behind Atletico Madrid's recent success and their upcoming Champions League match against Real Madrid. Since Simeone's leadership, Atletico Madrid has become one of Europe's most respected teams, having not lost to Real Madrid in six matches since their 2014 Champions League final loss. Torres emphasizes that Simeone drives the team by understanding their strengths and weaknesses, while also noting that Atletico must maintain consistency as they do not have the luxury of making up for lost points.

A light aircraft crash near a loch in western Scotland led to the discovery of two bodies among the wreckage. The plane was last seen traveling from central Scotland to Tiree, an island in the Inner Hebrides, and went missing around 30 miles east of Oban. Search and rescue efforts involved lifeboats, helicopters, and police, with the incident under investigation by the Procurator Fiscal.

A bus shattered the windscreen of a Boeing 777 passenger jet at Tashkent International Airport in Uzbekistan, causing significant damage but no known injuries; the busy airport, which handles the most passengers in Central Asia, experienced delays for numerous travelers. Such incidents are becoming increasingly frequent, including recent collisions between Ryanair planes at Dublin Airport and a British Airways plane hitting a hangar at Heathrow, highlighting the need for improved safety measures in airport operations.

An off-duty Secret Service agent named Arthur Baldwin was arrested in Washington D.C. for attempting to break into a house and causing property damage, leading to the revocation of his security clearance and his placement on leave. This incident occurred just two days after a high-ranking supervisor was placed on leave amid accusations of misconduct, both of which have tarnished the Secret Service's reputation. Additionally, an investigation is ongoing regarding an incident in March where two senior agency officials were found in a restricted area of the White House following alcohol consumption.

Israel is developing a unique tunnelling detection system, designed to accurately identify tunneling activities from a distance using advanced sensors, which reportedly eliminates false alarms. This system, developed by Elbit Systems in collaboration with the Israeli Ministry of Defense, follows extensive consideration of over 700 proposals aimed at addressing tunnel threats. The system, expected to cost approximately £2.3 million per mile for installation, could be deployed along the border between Gaza and Israel, though the exact timeline remains unclear.

A primary school headteacher in south London has banned all drinks except water during school hours to promote long-term pupil health, but some parents are campaigning against the rule, arguing it is too strict and goes against parental choice. The headteacher maintains support from most parents and students, while critics see it as unnecessary and even a "joke." This move follows similar bans at other schools, with health advocates like Tam Fry supporting restrictions on sugary drinks to encourage healthier habits among children.

Paul Smith has secured a significant fight against undefeated boxer Andre Ward on June 20 in Oakland, California. This match represents a major opportunity for Smith, who previously lost consecutive title challenges to Arthur Abraham, as Ward has not fought since November 2013. Both fighters express confidence in their abilities, with Smith eager to return to the ring and Ward determined to maintain his top form despite the long layoff.

German Chancellor Angela Merkel spent Easter on the island of Ischia in Italy, where she and her husband Joachim Sauer were staying at the five-star Miramare Spa Hotel. Despite the island being known for its warm climate, Merkel experienced cooler temperatures than usual, leading her to avoid sunbathing and instead opt for Pilates classes and spa treatments. Merkel's husband, a chemistry professor, maintained his low profile by avoiding the media and rarely accompanying her on their annual holiday.

Ander Herrera, a Manchester United midfielder, has scored multiple goals without looking at the ball or the goal, a unique and unusual skill that has caught attention recently. This behavior is most notable during matches against Aston Villa, where he scored two goals with his eyes shut, though he did maintain eye contact during a goal scored earlier in the season. Despite this talent, Manchester United manager Louis van Gaal has advised him to improve his technique by controlling the ball before shooting.

A 23-month-old toddler tragically died after her father accidentally struck her with a pickup truck in the driveway of their North Las Vegas home. The father and other family members were unaware that the toddler had wandered out of the house. The incident was ruled an accident, and no charges were filed.

The University of Connecticut baseball team has welcomed 5-year-old Grayson Hand, a child battling leukemia, as its newest member with the help of Team IMPACT. Grayson's involvement includes having his own locker and attending team practices and games, while his sister Sophie was named an honorary cheerleader. This partnership symbolizes the broader support network Grayson and his family have received during his battle against cancer.

A passenger on a London Midland train discovered excrement in a newspaper on the floor, causing severe delays and forcing the train to terminate early for cleaning. London Midland has vowed to provide police with CCTV footage of the suspect, describing the incident as "disgusting." The train service was delayed for several hours while the affected carriage was cleaned, and normal service resumed around 9:30 am.

James Rodriguez, the Colombian midfielder who moved to Real Madrid from Monaco for £60 million last summer, has proven to be a valuable asset to the team, winning 80% of matches when in the side compared to only 58% without him, according to Spanish newspaper Marca. Meanwhile, in other Spanish news, AS highlights Real Madrid's appeal despite Cristiano Ronaldo's controversial yellow card for diving against Rayo Vallecano. In Italian football news, La Gazzetta dello Sport reports that former Manchester City manager Roberto Mancini plans to make significant summer signings, aiming to add eight players to Inter Milan's squad from a list of 21 candidates.

A Florida man named Kenneth Crowder, who was believed to be under the influence of Flakka, a powerful and dangerous drug, attacked a police officer after being shocked with a Taser twice. During the incident, Crowder claimed he was God and attempted to stab the officer with a police badge, leading to his arrest and multiple charges including battery on a law-enforcement officer and assault with a deadly weapon. Flakka, similar in effects to a mix of crack cocaine and methamphetamine, has been linked to a rise in incidents in Florida, with over 670 occurrences in 2014 compared to just 85 in 2012.

During a Russian Premier League match between Arsenal Tula and Torpedo Moscow, a brawl by Torpedo fans led to the game being suspended for seven minutes. The fans broke down barriers and threw seats at law enforcement, resulting in the referee stopping the match. Torpedo Moscow went on to win the match 3-1, but the club faces severe punishment for the hooliganism, which is not their first such incident of fan violence this season.

High school girls in Huizhou, China, are undergoing military-style dagger drill training as part of their self-defense program under the guidance of a former special forces soldier. These girls, aged between 16 and 18, practice with non-harmful knives that have retractable blades, learning techniques that could potentially save their lives using any sharp object available. The training, which includes a series of eight defensive movements and lasts five days, is widely popular among the students who also chant "kill, stab, slash, and jab" during the sessions.

AP McCoy, the champion jockey who has held the title every year since 1997, is urging the nation to support his final Grand National ride with Shutthefrontdoor, with a potential £1 million prize and his retirement hanging in the balance. Reflecting on his career, McCoy acknowledges the unpredictability of the sport but remains hopeful for a fairytale ending. Despite his numerous successes, including winning the Grand National once, McCoy recognizes the challenge ahead and expresses his desire to achieve a second victory for a glorious conclusion to his record-breaking career.

John Isner advanced to the Miami Open semifinals with a straight-sets victory over Kei Nishikori, becoming the first American man to reach this stage since 2011. In the other semifinal, Andy Murray will face Tomas Berdych, with an interesting dynamic as Berdych is coached by someone who previously worked with Murray. Additionally, tensions between Isner and Nishikori were evident during their match, with Nishikori struggling against Isner's powerful serve.

Franz Beckenbauer, the German football legend, criticized Bayern Munich's performance in their Champions League quarter-final loss to Porto, likening it to players taking "sleeping pills." He specifically targeted defender Dante, comparing his performance to wearing "ski boots." Despite his harsh words, Beckenbauer remained optimistic about Bayern Munich's chances, suggesting they still have a chance to progress if they improve their performance.

A 21-year-old man named Arnold Quintero from San Antonio, Texas, has been arrested for sexually assaulting and physically abusing a 13-year-old girl, who was held captive and subjected to severe violence over several weeks. The girl described being beaten, forced to undress, and photographed by her attacker, who also sexually assaulted her. Quintero faces multiple charges including aggravated sexual assault of a child and possession with intent to deliver, among others.

In Week 12 of the Betway Premier League, Michael van Gerwen and Gary Anderson had mixed results, with both winning and losing one game each. Van Gerwen started strong by defeating James Wade 7-0 and securing a place in the May play-offs, but then lost to Gary Anderson. Anderson, after an initial loss to Stephen Bunting, won a high-scoring match against Van Gerwen with an impressive average of 105.94.

Training consultant Jay Rutland, husband of billionaire heiress Tamara Ecclestone, earned only £65 per week from his company Brigante Business Developments, which reported net assets of £3,378 for the year ending July 2014. Despite his modest income, the couple lives in a £45 million house and has access to expensive luxuries such as a Ferrari, Bentley, and private visits from Father Christmas. Jay Rutland's former career in the City of London ended in disgrace in 2012 due to market abuse allegations, and he faced a mugging shortly after his marriage to Tamara in 2013.

A 25-year-old man named Jia Binhui, diagnosed with leukemia in 2013, is using an unconventional home-made treatment involving hot coals to combat his cancer, as he cannot afford traditional medical treatment. Believing that temperatures over 42 degrees Celsius can kill cancer cells, Jia built a makeshift "barbecue" in his garden where he lies above the flames. Despite his desperate measures, Jia remains hopeful and recently married his long-term girlfriend, vowing to continue this unorthodox treatment before seeking further medical advice.

Leroy Fer, a Dutch midfielder for Queens Park Rangers, is set to return to the squad after recovering from a knee injury, potentially for the upcoming match against West Ham. Manager Chris Ramsey is considering giving Fer a chance despite concerns about his fitness level due to a previous injury and recent struggles with form. Additionally, the team is seeing other players return to fitness, such as Richard Dunne and Yun Suk-Young, while Rio Ferdinand remains out.

In the final kilometer of the Scheldeprijs race, Team Sky teammates Sir Bradley Wiggins and Geraint Thomas escaped a major crash, while their teammate Elia Viviani was injured, requiring hospital x-rays after hitting the barriers. Team Sky's sports director expressed relief that no other riders were involved in the crash and highlighted that despite the incident, the team remains in good shape for the upcoming Paris-Roubaix race. Alexander Kristoff of Katusha won the race, with only 14 riders competing in the sprint finish.

Before their FA Cup semi-final against Liverpool, Aston Villa's players received supportive messages in their dressing room at Wembley Stadium, with young star Jack Grealish sharing one from fan Mike Shenaniganz encouraging them to "put up with the rain to see the rainbow." Grealish's teammate, goalkeeper Brad Guzan, also shared a supportive message, urging the team to "fight like Lions." Manager Tim Sherwood included Grealish in the starting lineup following his recent strong performances.

A 12-year-old boy named Hanghang in central China suffered severe injuries when his old mobile phone exploded while charging, exposing part of his jawbone and embedding fragments in his arms and legs. The incident occurred when Hanghang used the phone as an alarm and noticed it was hot before it suddenly exploded, causing extensive bleeding. Experts attribute such explosions to issues with the battery, improper charging, or a short circuit, emphasizing the importance of proper phone usage and charging practices to prevent similar accidents.

Mike Rowe, known for his work on the show "Dirty Jobs," highlights the inspiring efforts of Chad Pregracke, the founder of Living Lands & Waters, who has dedicated over 20 years to cleaning U.S. waterways, collecting 8.4 million pounds of trash with the help of 87,000 volunteers. Pregracke's initiative earned him the 2013 CNN Hero of the Year Award, and he now aims to remove an additional 500,000 pounds of trash in 2015. Rowe’s segment showcases Pregracke’s innovative approach, including a solar-powered barge repurposed from a former strip club, which serves as both a home and office for the cleanup crew.

The ancient Tuscan town of Balestrino, dating back to the 11th century, was captured in a drone video showcasing its picturesque castle and deteriorating buildings. Seismic instability due to numerous historical earthquakes, including one measuring 6.7 on the Richter scale in 1887, led to the evacuation of its 800 inhabitants in 1953, leaving behind an eerie and hauntingly beautiful ghost town.

At a special event in Anaheim, California, director J.J. Abrams and the cast of "Star Wars: Episode VII — The Force Awakens" unveiled the trailer for the highly anticipated film, eliciting gasps, cheers, and applause from the audience. The event featured the introduction of new characters, including the droid BB-8, and revealed that much of the movie was filmed on actual sets rather than relying heavily on CGI. The first trailer concluded with a dramatic scene featuring Han Solo and Chewbacca, generating strong reactions from the audience.

Former Toronto Mayor Rob Ford announced plans for "very serious" surgery to remove a cancerous tumor in his abdomen, after chemotherapy and radiation treatments had shrunk the tumor to a more manageable size. Ford, who previously faced political challenges including a failed mayoral re-election bid and allegations of drug use, expressed gratitude for his support network and hoped to return to work in September. Despite the successful treatment, there remains a possibility of recurrence post-surgery.

The University of Cape Town in South Africa has removed a statue of Cecil Rhodes, a British colonialist, following weeks of student-led protests. The students, using the hashtag #RhodesMustFall, argued that Rhodes represented racism and should be removed to align with the university’s values. However, opponents argue that removing the statue erases history and advocate for more monuments to represent a full range of historical perspectives.

Michael Phelps returned to competitive swimming after a six-month suspension and won the 100 meters butterfly at the Arena Pro Swim Series in Arizona, finishing in 52.38 seconds. The 18-time Olympic gold medalist, who was banned following a drink-driving conviction, expressed joy at being back in competition but noted that he will miss the upcoming World Championships in Kazan. Phelps, aiming to compete in a fifth Olympics in Rio de Janeiro next year, is eager to continue his career despite facing challenges.

A woman's body was found hanging from a fire escape in Crown Heights, New York, for over an hour after she tragically took her own life. Witnesses were deeply affected, with one believing the scene was a Halloween prank due to the body being left exposed for such a prolonged period. Neighbors described her as a social and nice individual who struggled with mental health issues.

In a thrilling Rhone Valley derby, Lyon secured a 2-2 draw against Saint-Etienne, moving them to the top of Ligue 1 despite playing a man short. Meanwhile, Lille maintained their pursuit of a top-four finish by defeating Bordeaux 2-0, keeping themselves within four points of the fourth position. Additionally, Montpellier reclaimed their winning streak with a 1-0 victory over Caen thanks to an early goal from Brazilian defender Hilton.

Arsenal's manager, Arsene Wenger, was surprised by the key roles played by Hector Bellerin and Francis Coquelin in the team's recent push for the Premier League title. Bellerin, who previously struggled at Watford on loan, scored a crucial goal against Liverpool, while Coquelin, loaned out earlier in the season, has become a first-team regular. Wenger praised both players' performances, acknowledging their importance to the team despite initial doubts about their readiness for the top team.

Fox is developing a two-hour remake of the cult classic "The Rocky Horror Picture Show" for television, set to celebrate the film's 40th anniversary. Directed and choreographed by Kenneth Ortega, the special will be produced by Fox 21 Television Studios and The Jackal Group, with Gail Berman and Lou Adler as executive producers. This project follows previous attempts to adapt the musical into a TV special and comes after Fox aired a "Glee" episode featuring "Rocky Horror" songs in 2009.

Roma FC has been ordered to close part of their stadium for their next home game due to offensive banners displayed by supporters during a recent match against Napoli. These banners, which insulted the mother of a Napoli fan who died in violent clashes, were deemed provocative by a Serie A disciplinary tribunal. As a result, Roma's Stadio Olimpico will be partially closed for the upcoming league match against Atalanta on April 19.

Ellen White scored a spectacular goal for Notts County against her former team, Arsenal, by spinning and firing a free kick into the corner of the goal. This moment was particularly satisfying for White, as it combined scoring against her old team with the successful execution of a well-practiced set-piece from training. Despite this highlight, White later missed a penalty, and the game ended in a draw when Arsenal equalized late in the match.

Arsene Wenger reflects on his decision not to sign Eden Hazard in 2012, stating he has no regrets despite the Belgian star going on to have a successful career at Chelsea. Hazard, now a key player for Chelsea, is considered a leading candidate for the Premier League Player of the Year award, while Wenger believes Arsenal's Alexis Sanchez is also in contention. Wenger notes that Hazard has shown significant improvement in his game, becoming more effective in crucial moments.

Stephen Akers-Belcher, the Mayor of Hartlepool, was dismissed from his care manager role with Newcastle City Council after claiming to take time off for a funeral but being found at HMS Warrior instead. The council denied he was sacked for whistleblowing and stated that an investigation into his allegations found no misconduct. Akers-Belcher visited the historic warship 323 miles away from his work location, contradicting his claim of attending a local funeral.

Dr. John Parker, a humanitarian doctor who had been working in an Ebola treatment clinic in Sierra Leone, tested negative for the Ebola virus after developing flu-like symptoms and being taken to Westmead Hospital in Sydney. Dr. Parker had followed protocol and notified authorities upon returning from Sierra Leone. NSW Health confirmed the results, stating that no further testing for the virus was required.

A schoolboy named Frankie Franz, inspired by a trick shot by Barcelona's Martin Montoya, successfully replicated the 27-yard goal into a basketball hoop from the same distance, surprising both his mother and himself. At just nine years old, Frankie, who plays for Dagenham and Redbridge Football Club, demonstrated remarkable skill by replicating the trick shot on his first attempt in the garden. The boy, who dreams of playing for Real Madrid or Barcelona, showed exceptional confidence and talent, even managing to score again without being filmed.

The article highlights a selection of stunning cricket photographs that showcase the global appeal of the sport, ranging from amateur and professional players to children playing on a rubbish tip in Bangladesh. Among the images, Matthew Lewis's photograph of Dwayne Bravo making an extraordinary catch during the ICC World Twenty20 competition was crowned the winner of the Wisden–MCC Cricket Photograph of the Year 2014. The collection also includes a portrait of children playing cricket amidst foraging adults on a rubbish tip in Dhaka, Bangladesh, and a scene of players participating in "the world's highest game of cricket" atop Mount Kilimanjaro in Tanzania.

In a custody dispute, a New Jersey judge dismissed a father's claim that his ex-wife abused her parental discretion by taking their 11-year-old daughter to see P!nk's concert, ruling that the performances were appropriate for a preteen. The judge, after reviewing the case and speaking with the girl, concluded that the mother acted within reasonable bounds and did not put the child at risk. The judge highlighted that the concert, though containing suggestive elements, was not inappropriate given the daughter's age and the mother's due diligence in reviewing the content beforehand.

Salcombe, a coastal town in Devon, has surpassed London in average property prices, with the average cost of properties there reaching £671,759, compared to London's £638,217. Additionally, waterfront properties in Salcombe can cost up to £2 million, exceeding prices in some of London's most expensive areas such as Notting Hill and Regent's Park. As property values continue to rise in Salcombe by 10% annually, it has become a sought-after destination for both residents and tourists looking to enjoy its yachting and sailing paradise, fresh seafood, and stunning beaches.

Celtic Football Club has criticized the Scottish Football Association (SFA) over the ticket prices for their upcoming Scottish Cup semi-final against Inverness Caledonian Thistle at Hampden Park. Celtic argue that the North Stand ticket price of £23 is too high for many supporters, especially given that they are the majority attendees. The SFA defended its decision, stating that all four participating clubs were consulted and that the prices have remained the same for the past four years.

A 16-year-old student named Rebecca Rice was allowed to bring her pet Labrador, Holly, into her GCSE French oral exam to help calm her nerves. This unconventional solution was suggested by Rebecca’s teacher, Lorette Esteve, after other common stress-reduction tactics failed. Rebecca spent her five-minute exam period with Holly by her side, which reportedly helped significantly with her anxiety.

Anders Lindegaard, the struggling Manchester United goalkeeper, took advantage of the English weather to enjoy some leisure time with his wife Misse Beqiri. The couple, who tied the knot in a beach wedding in Mauritius and have a son together, shared a post on Lindegaard's Instagram page to highlight their relationship. Despite Lindegaard's limited playing time at Manchester United, his personal life remains a source of happiness and public affection.

Spanish goalkeepers David de Gea and Victor Valdes took a much-needed break from the pressures of the Premier League season by visiting a theme park in England, just days after Manchester United's victory over Manchester City. The team has shown strong form in recent weeks, with Manchester United now competing for a top-four finish in the league, after an earlier struggle. However, the uncertain futures of both goalkeepers could change their future sunny outings, with Valdes facing limited first-team opportunities since joining on a free transfer.

A 75-year-old piano teacher named John Goodwin, who was on trial for six counts of aggravated felonious sexual assault, shot himself outside a New Hampshire courthouse while jurors were deliberating the case. The former student, now 24, testified that he did not report the alleged assaults earlier due to embarrassment. Goodwin's lawyer argued that while his client was "touchy-feely," he did not commit a crime.

Amazon removed a controversial mobile game called "Rescue the Anorexia Girl" after it faced widespread criticism for its insensitive portrayal of anorexia. In the game, players were encouraged to throw food at a cartoon anorexic girl to prevent her from losing weight and dying, which many found offensive and stigmatizing. Critics argued that the game trivialized a serious mental illness and could discourage individuals from seeking help.

Scientists are working on creating an artificial brain modeled after the European Honeybee's cognitive abilities as part of the Green Brain Project, aiming to develop drones that can think, sense, and act like bees. Professor James Marshall believes that even creating a fraction of a bee’s capabilities would be a significant achievement, potentially leading to drones used for tasks such as crop pollination or search and rescue missions. So far, they have successfully replicated the vision portion of the bee's brain and are testing these capabilities in robotic drones in a specialized flying room at the University of Sheffield.

A newly-wed Air Malta crew member and her husband were celebrated with a unique post-wedding flight over the Mediterranean, where an Airbus A319 flew in the shape of two giant hearts shortly after takeoff. The unusual flight path was captured by flightradar24.com and was a surprise to many airline enthusiasts, but it was actually a romantic gesture to celebrate the marriage of a pilot and a cabin crew member. The flight also included the couple's family, friends, and colleagues on a short sight-seeing tour, with the arrival board at Malta International Airport noting the flight as "Just Married."

At a Norwegian zoo on Easter Monday, a five-year-old giraffe named Melvin died after being gored by an eland antelope in an enclosure. The tragic incident, which occurred when Melvin's head became stuck in the fence, was witnessed by around 30 people, including many children. Despite the quick response of zoo veterinarians, the injuries were too severe, and Melvin succumbed to his wounds shortly after the attack.

A restaurant manager in Leuven, Belgium, sparked outrage after charging a mother 36p to heat up her baby's feeding bottle, leading to a viral Twitter reaction. The mother, Gitte Denteneer, shared a picture of the bill on social media, describing it as a "very mean gesture." The Horeca Vlaanderen restaurant chain, which owns the Rubens Cafe, clarified that such charges are uncommon, stating that the service is typically free unless specifically mentioned otherwise.

North Korea has accused Mexico of illegally detaining one of its cargo ships, the Mu Du Bong, which ran aground off Mexico's coast in July. Mexico defended the detention, citing the shipowner's evasion of UN sanctions. Meanwhile, North Korea denied any wrongdoing and claimed that the crew members' human rights were being violated.

Prime Minister David Cameron plans to announce the provision of an additional 600,000 free childcare places per year, aimed at reducing the financial burden of childcare on working families and increasing employment opportunities. The Conservatives intend to fund these new places by reducing tax relief on pension contributions for higher earners. Cameron's speech emphasizes the party's commitment to rewarding hard work and reducing poverty through increased work incentives, with the new childcare policy expected to allow parents to work an extra 78 days a year without incurring childcare costs.

Manchester City secured their place in the Youth Cup final by scoring two late goals against Leicester City, extending their first-leg lead to 5-1 on aggregate. The goals came from substitutes Isaac Buckley and Brandon Barker, despite Layton Ndukwu giving Leicester hope with a penalty goal. This sets up a clash with Chelsea in the final, which will take place at the City Football Academy Stadium in the first leg on April 20, followed by a trip to Stamford Bridge on April 27.

During a nationally broadcast Q&A session, Russian President Vladimir Putin dismissed the impact of Western sanctions, stating they are about constraining Russia's development rather than just concerning Ukraine and Crimea.
