Additionally, a startup called Salt offers a credit-card sized device that automatically unlocks smartphones within a ten-foot range and relocks them when the user moves away, aiming to save users about 53 hours annually by reducing manual unlocking tasks.

Belinda, a 56-year-old from Essex, regrets undergoing a facelift in Turkey after the procedure left her ears sewn awkwardly to the side of her face. The botched surgery was featured on TLC's "Extreme Beauty Disasters," aiming to warn against the risks of low-cost foreign cosmetic procedures. Following the initial failure, a plastic surgeon corrected some of the damage, though Belinda required additional surgeries to fully address the issues.

Labour's shadow business secretary, Chuka Umunna, criticized UKIP, claiming it "hates modern Britain" and is infected with a "virus of racism," following controversial remarks by UKIP leader Nigel Farage about the ethnicity of UKIP supporters and candidates. This criticism came after UKIP was accused of association with far-right campaigners, including Gary Field, a former organizer of the English Defence League, who attended a UKIP event in Broadstairs. Umunna argued that UKIP's leader does not understand race in modern Britain and lacks the necessary support to combat racism within the party.

Supermodel Maggie Rizer, who recently gave birth to her third child, a daughter named Cecilia, has returned to her fit and toned physique just nine weeks after giving birth, as evidenced by photos she shared on Instagram of her playing on the beach with her young son. Maggie, who continues to share updates about her family on social media, also posted pictures of herself working out on a Pilates reformer two weeks before her beach vacation. Despite stepping away from modeling in 2004 due to financial losses, Maggie remains active and engaged with her family, using her platform to raise awareness about AIDS.

The average Briton consumes about four servings of cheese per week, with cheddar being the most popular variety at 80%, followed by mozzarella and red Leicester. According to a survey, one in four cheese lovers eat melted cheese with everything, while a third enjoy their cheese with pickles, and many reach for cheese sandwiches when hungry. The survey also found that 32% of office workers eat the same lunch daily for nearly four and a half years, highlighting a preference for routine and stability in their diet.

A dress worn by Vivien Leigh as Scarlett O'Hara in the 1939 film "Gone With the Wind" was auctioned for $137,000. This ensemble, originally slate blue-gray, had faded to light gray due to age. The dress was part of a collection amassed by James Tumblin, a former Universal Studios makeup department head, who purchased it for just $20 from the studio's trash. Other notable items from the same collection also sold well, including a hat worn by Leigh and trousers from Clark Gable's suit, fetching up to $55,000 each.

A Turkish Airlines flight from Milan to Istanbul made an emergency landing at Atatürk Airport after its engine caught fire, resulting in the evacuation of all 97 passengers without injury. The incident followed other recent emergencies involving Turkish Airlines, including a bomb threat on another flight out of Istanbul. After landing, the plane's right engine was found to be severely damaged, and an investigation into the cause of the incident has begun.

Adam Leheup, a 34-year-old architect from Surrey, was cleared of rape and sexual assault by a jury at Blackfriars Crown Court. The case involved a 25-year-old woman he met through a dating app; during a night-long date, Leheup claimed they mutually enjoyed physical intimacy, while the woman alleged he forced himself upon her without her consent. After a week-long trial, the jury found Leheup not guilty of both charges, and he was released from court.

Italian artist AleXsandro Palombo launched the "What Kind Of Man Are You?" campaign, encouraging women to write their thoughts on gender violence on their underwear and share via social media as part of the #briefmessage campaign. The initiative aims to raise awareness about gender violence and challenge machismo, with messages ranging from defiant statements to simple anti-violence slogans. Palombo hopes this will contribute to cultural and social education to combat gender violence.

Nick Clegg faced criticism over his broken tuition fees promise during a campaign stop in Surbiton, where he was heckled by protesters. Clegg criticized Chancellor George Osborne's austerity measures, calling him "a very dangerous man" who would destroy public services through ideologically rigid policies. Clegg also distinguished between Conservative leaders, describing David Cameron as a "classic traditional shire Tory" he could work with, while emphasizing the need for his Liberal Democrat party to remain in power to counter Osborne’s plans.

Sharon Edwards, a 55-year-old teacher, has been missing for nearly a month, and her family is struggling to cope with the uncertainty of her disappearance. Last seen leaving a hotel in Grafton, NSW, around 10 PM on March 14, Ms. Edwards has not been seen since, and police are treating the case as a potential homicide. Despite extensive searches and forensic examinations of her properties, her family and investigators remain hopeful that she will be found.

Steven Nelms, a husband from Plano, Texas, wrote an essay to celebrate his wife Glorianna's contributions as a stay-at-home mother while acknowledging the financial strain it places on his family. In the essay, he breaks down the monetary value of her domestic work, estimating her annual salary to be approximately $73,960, and expresses his inability to afford her role financially. Nelms also admits to feeling ashamed at times when his wife felt she didn't have equal rights to their shared income and promises to better appreciate her invaluable contributions.

David Cameron defended his election campaign against criticism, emphasizing his focus on economic stability and practical issues like jobs and childcare rather than political excitement. Meanwhile, there are reports of internal Tory dissatisfaction, with some figures considering a leadership change for Cameron post-election if the Conservatives lose, favoring Boris Johnson as the successor. Additionally, a significant donor has criticized Cameron's campaign strategy, suggesting it lacks passion and vision, potentially jeopardizing the Conservative Party's chances in the upcoming election.

Six city officials in Parma, Missouri, resigned shortly after a black mayor, Tyus Byrd, was elected. Trish Cohen, the former police chief, and Rich Medley, the former assistant police chief, stated they feared for their safety due to threats against their homes made by Byrd's family members. Meanwhile, Byrd denied knowing the reasons for the resignations and claimed that race did not play a role, stating she had never mentioned firing anyone or interfering with the police.

Swedish photographer Johan Bavman documented the experiences of fathers taking full advantage of Sweden’s generous parental leave policy through his photography project. Sweden offers 480 days of parental leave, with 390 days paid at 80% of income, and mandates that at least 60 of these days must be shared between parents to promote gender equality. While only 12% of Swedish couples equally share the leave, Bavman’s project highlights the devotion and challenges faced by these fathers, aiming to provide role models that others can relate to.

Tragically, two 18-month-old twin boys, Eli and Silas Keslar, drowned in a canal in Arizona after their mother was distracted by a bee and lost hold of their stroller. Despite the mother's desperate attempts to rescue them, the boys were found an hour later and pronounced dead at the hospital. A Go Fund Me page was established to cover memorial and medical costs, raising over $20,000.

Arsenal manager Arsene Wenger is considering offering Abou Diaby a new contract despite the midfielder's history of injuries, which have kept him out of action for over two years. Diaby recently returned to training after a bout of injury but has only made 22 appearances in the past five seasons. Additionally, Wenger hopes to extend contracts for club captain Mikel Arteta and veteran player Tomas Rosicky, though no specific timelines or conditions were provided. Diaby's injury record, which includes 42 injuries since joining Arsenal in 2006, is extensive, with an average of one injury every 79.5 days.

Eden Hazard has emerged as the Premier League's standout player this season, demonstrating significant growth in his role as a crucial figure for Chelsea, often delivering winning performances even when the team isn't at its best. His improved finishing skills, evident in Chelsea's 1-0 victory, have transformed him into a primary threat in attacks, making him an indispensable asset for both his team and potential future Champions League success. Meanwhile, Manchester United, despite their possession dominance, struggled to create clear-cut chances, highlighting the importance of key individual performances like those from Hazard in securing victories.

President Obama and Cuban leader Raul Castro met at a dinner during the Summit of the Americas in Panama City, marking the first high-level meeting between the two nations in over five decades and symbolizing a significant thaw in their long-standing diplomatic tensions. This historic encounter was part of broader efforts to normalize relations, including the potential removal of Cuba from the U.S. list of state sponsors of terrorism and the anticipated reopening of embassies. The meeting also reflected the broader diplomatic shift, though it faced some opposition from U.S. lawmakers who viewed the engagement with the Cuban government unfavorably.

Latisha Fisher, a 35-year-old mother with a history of psychiatric issues and violence, was charged with second-degree murder after allegedly smothering her 20-month-old son, Gavriel, in a restaurant bathroom in Manhattan. Fisher told police she feared someone would eat the child, leading her to take such extreme action. Recent evaluations showed Fisher was considered mentally fit, though she had a history of violent incidents and was previously diagnosed with schizophrenia following a stabbing.

At the Star Wars: Episode VII - The Force Awakens panel in Anaheim, Carrie Fisher and Mark Hamill appeared alongside Daisy Ridley, John Boyega, and Oscar Isaac, while Harrison Ford, though mentioned, was absent due to recovering from a March plane crash. The panel showcased the new trailer, featuring the return of iconic characters and the introduction of new faces, and highlighted the film's setting on a new desert planet named Jaku. Director JJ Abrams and producer Kathleen Kennedy praised Ford’s heroic actions and expressed his continued involvement in the film despite his absence.

Bill Nye "the Science Guy" accompanied President Barack Obama on an Earth Day excursion to the Florida Everglades via Air Force One, where Nye engaged with the press about his love for jet fuel. During the 1,836-mile round-trip flight, Nye and Obama aimed to promote efforts to cut carbon pollution and preserve the environment, though some questioned the environmental impact of such a long flight. The trip was part of broader initiatives by the administration to address climate change and secure the Everglades.

Floyd Mayweather Jr. reflects on his independence in the boxing world, recalling how his friends initially thought he was crazy when he left promoter Bob Arum to organize his own fight against Manny Pacquiao, which would become the richest boxing match ever. Mayweather, now set to earn over $180 million from the event, sees the fight not just as a financial opportunity but as a chance to cement his legacy as one of the greatest boxers of all time. Despite the immense pressure and hype surrounding the match, Mayweather remains calm and confident, believing that his calculated approach and experience will be enough to secure victory.

Elderflower Fields is a family-oriented festival held annually in the picturesque Pippingford Park in Ashdown Forest, offering a mix of outdoor activities, music, and luxury camping. Created by a group of friends in 2012, the festival aims to provide a unique and inspiring experience for both children and adults, with a wide range of activities including sports, music, arts, and environmental engagement. In 2015, the festival partners with East Sussex Music Services to offer music workshops and performances, along with various sports and artistic camps, making it a comprehensive destination for families seeking an enriching weekend away.

Six Chelsea players were selected for the Professional Footballers' Association (PFA) Premier League team of the year, reflecting their dominant performance in the 2014-15 season. Key contributors include defenders Branislav Ivanovic, John Terry, and Gary Cahill, as well as midfielders Eden Hazard and Nemanja Matic, and striker Diego Costa. Tottenham's Harry Kane was the sole English forward in the team, alongside Costa up front.

Two young friends, Michael Owen and Kyle Careford, tragically lost their lives in a car crash that occurred in Crowborough, East Sussex, shortly after Michael received news of a job offer and was preparing for his daughter's fifth birthday. Michael, 21, was a responsible father to his 5-year-old daughter Lily-Rose, while Kyle, also 21, was close to turning 21. Local tributes and flowers have been left at the crash site, and friends and family have expressed their grief and admiration for the men.

The article discusses Manchester City's struggle to establish themselves as a top European force despite financial success, highlighting issues with the current manager, player signings, and fan apathy. Critics argue that Manchester City needs to make bolder moves in terms of both management and player acquisitions to achieve genuine greatness and compete at the highest level. The piece suggests that unless Manchester City thinks bigger and aspires to true dominance, they will remain in the shadows of other elite clubs.

Kim Callaghan, a mother of two from Ardee, County Louth, Ireland, dramatically lost over ten stone by switching to a healthier diet and regular exercise, transforming from a size 28 to a size 8. Initially, her weight made her feel masculine and she feared losing her femininity, leading her to wear baggy clothing. Her turning point came when she couldn't keep up with her children on a walk, prompting her to join Slimming World secretly and eventually sharing her progress with her family. Kim now enjoys a more active lifestyle and a much healthier wardrobe, feeling both healthy and feminine.

The Miami-Dade Police Department conducted a hidden camera operation at Miami International Airport, catching baggage handlers stealing from passengers' bags, as part of an ongoing investigation into luggage theft by airport workers. This issue is not unique to Miami, as a CNN analysis of TSA claims from 2010 to 2014 revealed over 30,000 claims of missing valuables from checked luggage across multiple major U.S. airports. Efforts to combat the problem include increased screening and aggressive investigations, but the issue remains a significant concern for airport security and law enforcement.

Marla McCants, an 800-pound woman from Nashville, Tennessee, was finally able to stand for the first time in years after her daughters begged a doctor to help her overcome her refusal to cooperate with medical treatment. This pivotal moment, which occurred after Marla was discharged from the hospital due to her non-cooperation, marked a significant turning point in her weight loss journey. Marla's determination to stand, spurred by the realization that she was running out of time, led to her successful surgery and gradual weight loss, culminating in her ability to stand on a scale for the first time in five years.

Nasa's Curiosity rover has discovered that liquid water could exist on the surface of Mars due to the presence of perchlorate salts, which lower the freezing point of water. This finding, published in the journal Nature, suggests that ancient lakes may have existed in the Gale Crater, where Curiosity landed in 2012. Additionally, observations indicate that water vapor in the Martian atmosphere can condense on the surface at night, forming briny liquid water through interaction with perchlorate salts.

An 11-year-old boy named Luke Shambrook has been missing from a campsite in Victoria for four days, prompting an extensive search effort involving police, emergency crews, and volunteers. Despite challenging conditions, authorities remain hopeful that Luke is still alive and are focusing their search in the bushland around Lake Eildon. Luke, who is autistic, has a high pain tolerance and may not realize he is lost, which complicates the search but does not diminish the hope of finding him.

Nicola Sturgeon announced that she would support calls for all tax powers to be devolved to Scotland "as soon as possible," despite warnings from Labour leader Jim Murphy that this could create a £7.6 billion budget shortfall. The debate highlighted the tension between the SNP's push for fiscal autonomy and the financial challenges it would pose, particularly given the decline in North Sea oil revenues. Other leaders criticized Sturgeon for potentially breaking promises regarding a "once-in-a-generation" referendum and for the SNP's stance on immigration and foreign aid.

The Royal Commission into Institutional Responses to Child Sex Abuse in Rockhampton, Australia, has heard disturbing accounts of abuse at the Neerkol St Joseph's Orphanage, including sexual assaults with objects, forced pregnancies, and severe physical punishments. Victims, such as AYL, detailed multiple instances of rape and other forms of abuse by staff members, while others like Mary Adams described physical and emotional maltreatment. The commission is examining historical allegations of child abuse at the orphanage, which operated from 1885 to 1978, and has heard from several former residents who endured horrific conditions.

Churchill Downs, the famous racetrack hosting the Kentucky Derby, has banned the use of selfie sticks for the 141st running of the event on May 2nd, joining a growing list of venues that have restricted these devices to ensure safety. The ban extends beyond Derby Day to cover all live racing events at the track. The move aims to protect both the horses and spectators, addressing concerns about potential hazards posed by the extended reach of selfie sticks in crowded spaces.

Mercedes-Benz Fashion Week Australia concluded with the Johanna Johnson show, showcasing Hollywood-inspired designs. The week highlighted various trends such as voluminous silhouettes, metallic fabrics, and sheer, revealing garments, alongside bold makeup and unconventional accessories that often overshadowed the clothing. Notable trends included big, voluminous dresses, comfortable and slouchy styles, and daring, revealing designs that pushed boundaries.

Prince William, who recently started his job as a pilot for East Anglian Air Ambulance, will take his full two-week paternity leave when his second child is born later in April. Meanwhile, the Duchess of Cambridge, who is expected to give birth at the Lindo Wing of St Mary’s Hospital, will largely remain at their London home during her maternity leave, avoiding a potential media frenzy. Both parents plan to keep the birth announcement private until the next morning to avoid unnecessary attention.

Leanne Kenny, a 23-year-old from Northwich, Cheshire, gained significant weight due to eating discounted junk food at her supermarket job, reaching almost 20 stone. After a breaking point where she couldn't fit into the largest dress in a store, Leanne decided to lose weight and adopted a healthier lifestyle, joining Weight Watchers and focusing on walking, ultimately losing seven stone. She now weighs 13 stone and plans to continue her fitness journey to reach her goal of a size 12 by summer.

Ed Balls, the shadow chancellor, dismissed as a "joke" an infamous 2010 note from Liam Byrne, a former Labour minister, which admitted the party had blown the nation’s finances. This note, left in the Treasury by Byrne, has long been used by opponents to criticize Labour’s fiscal management. Balls defended Labour’s current economic plans, stating that their manifesto would reduce the deficit without requiring additional borrowing, while also blaming the leak on a Conservative colleague.

Prosecutors dropped a series of cases against journalists accused of paying public officials for information, following a jury's acquittal of nine reporters in a high-profile case. This decision, which marks a significant U-turn, was influenced by criticisms of the application of the archaic "misconduct in public office" law and the public's lack of support for jailing journalists who expose matters of public interest. The move leaves Operation Elveden, the tainted Metropolitan Police probe into tabloid journalists, in disarray, with 23 out of 27 journalists cleared or having their cases dropped.

The article discusses the controversial practice of offering female sterilization as part of plea deals in criminal cases, highlighting its historical context and comparing it to past eugenic practices. While such practices are now widely considered unethical, the article questions whether they remain constitutional under modern standards, noting that individuals can waive their Eighth Amendment rights to avoid cruel and unusual punishments. The piece also explores the gender bias involved, suggesting that the practice is more controversial when applied to women due to societal attitudes and the relative rarity of such cases involving women.

A federal judge has sentenced former Blackwater security guard Nicholas Slatten to life in prison for his role in a 2007 shooting that killed 14 Iraqi civilians and wounded 17 others, while three other guards received 30 years and one day in prison for similar charges. The sentences were handed down after a day-long hearing where defense lawyers argued for leniency and prosecutors sought harsher penalties. The case, which has spanned years, involved a controversial mass shooting in Nisour Square, Baghdad, where the guards were convicted of multiple manslaughter and firearms charges despite defense claims of self-defense.

Four men accused of theft were brutally beheaded and displayed in Mosul by ISIS militants, marking a more severe punishment than usual for such crimes. U.S.-led forces conducted airstrikes targeting ISIS positions in Iraq and Syria, while Iraq's Prime Minister vowed to protect civilians' rights when territories under ISIS control are reclaimed. The recent victories against ISIS in Tikrit have led to the excavation of mass graves containing the remains of soldiers killed by the militants, highlighting the scale of the conflict and its human cost.

Shadow Business Secretary Chuka Umunna has expressed opposition to maintaining the 50p top rate of income tax permanently, suggesting it should be a temporary measure focused on deficit reduction rather than a moral stance. This position highlights internal divisions within the Labour Party regarding the continuation of the 50p tax rate, with other Labour figures like Shadow Chancellor Ed Balls advocating for its temporary nature. Umunna also emphasized the need for a more positive and confident approach to deficit reduction to counter potential leftist opposition if Labour were to form the next government.

Bristol City secured their promotion to the Championship by defeating Bradford City 6-0, becoming the first team in Sky Bet League One to mathematically confirm their promotion. This achievement comes after a remarkable season that included winning the Johnstone’s Paint Trophy and consistently leading the league, with key contributions from defender Aden Flint, who scored 11 goals and celebrated by winning the trophy at Wembley. Bristol City's owner plans to renovate their home stadium to accommodate 27,000 spectators, positioning the club for potential further success in higher divisions.

The article discusses how the Kardashian family's visit to Armenia brought renewed attention to the Armenian Genocide, a historical event that was often overlooked or minimized. It highlights the impact of celebrity involvement in raising awareness about this humanitarian crime and the ongoing efforts of the Armenian community to gain recognition for the genocide. The piece also touches on the complex relationship between Armenians and the descendants of those who participated in the events of 1915, emphasizing the hope for healing through increased dialogue and acknowledgment.

Janet Street-Porter, a Scottish journalist, posted a tweet comparing someone she met to Nicola Sturgeon, Scotland's First Minister, and faced a flood of hostile responses from Sturgeon's supporters. This incident highlights the intense loyalty and protection of Sturgeon among her followers, who view any criticism as unforgivable. The article also explores how Sturgeon, despite her political success and the admiration of her supporters, has become a figure almost untouchable, with her critics facing harsh backlash, suggesting a form of political cultism.

England's traveling fans sang anti-IRA songs during a friendly match against Italy, which embarrassed the FA and strained relations with the host country. The Football Association faces a dilemma in addressing fan behavior while also managing a policy that rewards travel to matches with greater access to tickets for major tournaments. The incident highlights the ongoing challenges in balancing fan enthusiasm with maintaining a respectful and inclusive atmosphere for international fixtures.

Arkansas Governor Asa Hutchinson has decided not to sign a recently passed religious freedom bill into law, instead returning it to the state legislature for amendments. Hutchinson cited his son Seth's influence and concerns over the bill's potential to be misused to discriminate against LGBTQ individuals. The governor expressed a desire to align the bill more closely with the 1993 federal Religious Freedom Restoration Act, which critics argue better protected the rights of gays and lesbians.

Hillary Clinton's announcement of her 2016 presidential candidacy has brought renewed attention to gender equality in U.S. politics, placing her success or failure under significant scrutiny. A win could mark a crucial step towards women's full political inclusion, while a loss could reinforce stereotypes about women's electability. Regardless of the outcome, Clinton's candidacy serves as a pivotal moment for assessing progress on gender equality, highlighting the unique challenges faced by female presidential candidates.

The Clinton Foundation has decided to continue accepting donations from foreign governments, but with restrictions, despite the potential conflict of interest given that Hillary Clinton is now running for president. The foundation will limit these donations to only six countries: Australia, Canada, Germany, the Netherlands, Norway, and the United Kingdom, while halting direct contributions from others and ending foreign government sponsorship of programs. In response to criticism, the foundation will now disclose its donors quarterly rather than annually.

Many popular brands are reducing the size of their products without decreasing the price, a practice known as "shrinkflation." This trend includes items like Cadbury's Fingers, Creme Eggs, and various household goods, leaving consumers feeling they are getting less for the same amount of money. Critics argue that this tactic confuses shoppers and undermines trust in consumer goods, while supporters suggest it helps support government health initiatives by encouraging people to buy smaller portions.

St George's Day was celebrated across the UK with patriotic parades, veteran marches, and Morris dancing in the warm spring weather. Events included the Nottingham St George's Day Parade and a 70th-anniversary parade in Emsworth, Hampshire, marking the end of World War II. Despite the pleasant temperatures, forecasters predicted a return to cooler and wetter weather over the weekend.

Manchester City secured a comfortable victory against West Ham at the Etihad Stadium, thanks to an own goal by James Collins and a goal by Sergio Aguero, with Aguero reaching 20 Premier League goals for the season. The match report highlights strong performances from Manchester City players like Pablo Zabaleta, Eliaquim Mangala, and Jesus Navas, while West Ham struggled to make an impact, with only a few standout performances noted, such as Carl Jenkinson's interception.

Andy Murray and Kim Sears are set to marry in Dunblane, Scotland, with decorations reminiscent of the royal wedding of Prince William and Kate Middleton, including trees lining the aisle at Dunblane Cathedral. The town is buzzing with excitement, with local businesses and residents decorating their spaces and sending gifts to the couple. The wedding will feature a mix of close family and friends, with notable attendees including former tennis star Tim Henman, but no major celebrities are expected to attend.

Andy Murray, despite a strong performance against Novak Djokovic in the Miami Open final, lost in a three-set match, marking his seventh consecutive defeat to Djokovic. The match was particularly grueling due to the intense heat, with Djokovic showing signs of frustration, including yelling at a ball kid. Murray, who recently returned to world No. 3, acknowledged the need to find a strategy to better compete against Djokovic, while Djokovic extended his ranking streak to 141 weeks, tying him with Rafael Nadal for sixth place on the all-time list.

The Siezen family transformed a large truck into a colorful and cozy home complete with turrets and a rooftop bathtub, perfect for their nomadic lifestyle. Justin and Jola, whose job as acrobats requires frequent travel, turned their truck into a mobile home that meets road requirements while offering a unique living space. Inside, the home features a spacious kitchen, a fold-out baby chair, and cleverly designed storage solutions, all while maintaining a whimsical and artistic atmosphere.

A 26-year-old Mexican woman named Elizabeth Elena Laguna Salgado went missing from Provo, Utah, on April 16th, and despite no evidence of kidnapping, she has not been in contact with her family or been seen since. Her uncle, along with kidnapping survivor Elizabeth Smart and her father, have joined efforts to find her, emphasizing the importance of public awareness and vigilance. Laguna Salgado is described as a strikingly beautiful woman with long black hair, brown eyes, and standing at 5 feet 4 inches tall, last seen wearing a denim jacket and blue jeans.

World heavyweight boxing champion Wladimir Klitschko, while focused on his upcoming title defense against Bryant Jennings, remains deeply concerned about the ongoing conflict in Ukraine. Klitschko, who has a political role in Ukraine, expresses his shock and dismay at the situation, emphasizing the importance of achieving a peaceful resolution and maintaining democracy. He believes that with international support, Ukraine can move away from a Soviet-style dictatorship and toward a democratic future.

A 21-year-old woman named Jamyra Gallmon, who attended a prestigious military academy, has been arrested and charged with the first-degree felony murder of 30-year-old David Messerschmitt, a Washington D.C. lawyer, who was found dead in his hotel room after being stabbed. Surveillance video showed Gallmon entering the hotel shortly after Messerschmitt's last known communication with his wife. Police believe the motive may have been robbery, though Gallmon's mother stated that her daughter had never been in trouble before and had ambitions to join the military.

The article discusses the controversial idea that a woman's hormones might make her unfit to be president, as suggested by a Texas businesswoman who believes Hillary Clinton's hormones would make her likely to start unnecessary wars. It contrasts this viewpoint with research indicating that women leaders tend to take fewer unnecessary risks compared to men. The piece also highlights the broader issue of gender bias in the workplace and its impact on women's career advancement, emphasizing that such biases hinder not just individual women but society as a whole.

Valerie Cadman-Khan, a mother of five, successfully sued Cleveland Police for wrongful arrest after she was handcuffed in front of her 12-year-old daughter Aimee during a false allegation of child neglect. Despite winning the case and receiving compensation, Cadman-Khan has not yet received an official apology from the police. The incident, which involved accusations of leaving Aimee unattended in the cold, led to Cadman-Khan being arrested and taken away from her daughter, an experience she found deeply traumatic and humiliating.

Richard Kerr, a 53-year-old survivor of child abuse, claims that he and two other boys were trafficked from a children's home in Belfast to London in the 1970s, where they were allegedly abused by high-profile individuals in a pedophile ring connected to Dolphin Square and Elm Guest House. These claims provide new evidence linking alleged pedophile rings in London and Northern Ireland and may strengthen the case for an official inquiry into the abuse at the Kincora children's home.

James Schoenfeld, one of the three kidnappers involved in the infamous 1976 Chowchilla bus kidnapping, was granted parole 39 years after the crime, following the inspiration from the film "Dirty Harry." The kidnapping, where 26 children and a bus driver were held in an underground trailer, led to a $5 million ransom demand and ended with the captives escaping unharmed. Despite the parole, the victims of the kidnapping expressed strong opposition to Schoenfeld's release, citing the lasting trauma from the experience.

California Governor Jerry Brown has mandated a 25% reduction in urban water usage across the state in response to ongoing drought conditions, despite reservoirs currently holding a year's supply of water. This directive targets various sectors including residential areas, golf courses, and businesses, while exempting agriculture, which uses 80% of the state’s water. As the fourth consecutive summer of drought looms, some communities are adapting by removing lawns and planting drought-resistant vegetation, while others remain resistant to change.

Geordie Shore star Charlotte Cosby has lost over two and a half stone, but her recent photos have drawn criticism for appearing too thin, sparking concerns about her health and potentially harmful dieting practices. Other cast members like Vicky Pattison, Holly Hagan, and Marnie Simpson have also lost significant weight, facing similar scrutiny. Medical expert Dr. Marilyn Glenville warns that rapid weight loss can lead to health issues and recommends tailored, sustainable approaches to weight management.

A new campaign from Rape Crisis London, known as #ThisDoesn'tMeanYes, aims to combat the myth that women are responsible for rape due to their clothing choices, showcasing 2,000 images of women in various outfits to emphasize that no outfit means consent. This initiative follows similar efforts by the Crown Prosecution Service to challenge societal views that blame victims for their actions, such as drinking or wearing provocative clothing. Despite progress, recent surveys indicate that a significant portion of the younger generation still believes that victims are partly responsible for their assault if they were intoxicated.

Leonie Granger, a former care worker, was found guilty of manslaughter in the death of Mehmet Hassan, a professional gambler, after she lured him to his death with the help of her boyfriend and a friend. The three conspirators used a honeytrap scheme, where Granger befriended Hassan and led him back to his flat, allowing his killers to tie him up and kick him to death in search of hidden winnings. Granger, along with her boyfriend Kyrron Jackson and friend Nicholas Chandler, were also found guilty of multiple related offenses including robbery and false imprisonment.

David Cameron plans to implement a policy requiring children who fail their English and math tests at age 11 to retake them in their first year of secondary school at age 12. This decision, affecting around 100,000 pupils annually, aims to ensure these students can catch up on essential reading, writing, and arithmetic skills. The policy is part of the Conservatives' strategy to improve educational outcomes and prepare students better for secondary education and beyond.

Jonathan Trott had a significant comeback, scoring 72 runs in a practice match against St Kitts, after suffering a brutal performance during the previous Ashes tour. He reunited with Alastair Cook, who contributed an unbeaten 95, in a comfortable Test match setup, showcasing their improved form and potential partnership for the upcoming Antigua Test. England's team demonstrated a dominant display, with notable performances from Ben Stokes and the overall improvement in their batting and bowling, indicating a strong start to their Caribbean tour.

Ed Miliband announced a series of housing policies aimed at making homeownership more accessible, including scrapping stamp duty for first-time buyers and giving local people priority for new homes, which led to a drop in the share values of leading housebuilders. These measures, such as banning landhoarding and imposing higher taxes on foreign buyers, have been met with criticism from other political parties who argue that the proposals are unfunded and potentially damaging to the housing market. Meanwhile, opposition parties like the Conservatives and Liberal Democrats have criticized Labour's plans, suggesting they are unrealistic or likely to fail.

Former President George W. Bush surprised many by criticizing President Barack Obama's foreign policy, particularly regarding the lifting of sanctions on Iran and the ongoing nuclear deal negotiations. At a closed-door meeting with Jewish donors in Las Vegas, Bush expressed deep concerns about the potential negative impacts on US national security and suggested that Obama's approach to the Islamic State was failing. These remarks contrasted sharply with Obama's optimistic view of the deal as the "best bet" to prevent Iran from obtaining a nuclear weapon.

A husband was awarded £9,000 in compensation for nervous shock after his wife, Julie Ronayne, suffered severe swelling following a botched hysterectomy at Liverpool Women's Hospital. The case, which could have significant financial implications for the NHS, is being appealed by the health trust, fearing it could lead to a flood of similar claims. The appeal centers on whether a relative can be considered a "secondary victim" and be awarded compensation based solely on witnessing a loved one's traumatic condition, without proving they suffered from psychiatric injury.

Bruce Jenner is set to launch an eight-episode docu-series on E! detailing his gender transition journey, but his sons Burt, Brandon, and Brody, along with stepdaughter Kim Kardashian, are cautioning him against revealing too much due to concerns it might undermine his accomplishments. Despite some reservations, Jenner's children generally support him, with Kim praising his courage and honesty. The series, produced in consultation with GLAAD, aims to educate and foster empathy but faces criticism from some who feel Jenner’s newfound supporters were not always supportive.

The article highlights several tourist destinations known for their breathtaking views, ranging from the CN Tower in Toronto with its glass floor and edge-walking experience to the Grand Canyon Skywalk in Arizona, providing visitors with stunning vistas over the Grand Canyon. Other notable locations include Pulpit Rock in Norway, offering panoramic views after a challenging hike, and the Tokyo Skytree in Japan, standing at 2,080 feet and featuring observation decks and amenities. These sites attract millions of visitors annually, each presenting unique challenges and rewards for those seeking memorable views.

Mark Wood, a 25-year-old uncapped English fast bowler, has been selected for the upcoming Test series against West Indies, despite his non-traditional physique and past injuries. Known for his surprising bowling style and reverse swing abilities, Wood has improved his performance and fitness, allowing him to play consistently and earn his spot in the national team. He plans to seize the opportunity to perform well and contribute to England's cricket efforts in the Caribbean.

A Scottish mother, Dawn Williamson, was cured of her 30-year phobia of snakes on live television during an episode of ITV1's This Morning, with the process taking just ten minutes. Therapists Nik and Eva Speakman successfully challenged Dawn's irrational fear by demonstrating its irrationality and helping her confront her phobia head-on, allowing her to touch and even stroke a large Burmese python. This was the first time viewers witnessed the therapy process in real-time, with the Speakmans having previously treated 60 others with similar phobias through similar methods.

Apple has acquired Israeli company Link Computational Imaging for $20 million, a move that suggests the tech giant is looking to enhance camera technology in upcoming iPhone and iPad models. Link's multi-aperture cameras, capable of depth-sensing and allowing for post-capture refocusing, could significantly improve smartphone photography capabilities. Apple has been hinting at camera upgrades and has launched a marketing campaign highlighting the quality of its current camera technology, featuring images shot exclusively on iPhone 6 devices.

Chris Ramsey, the interim manager of QPR, has expressed his commitment to the club, stating he will stay for as long as they want him, regardless of their league position next season. Ramsey, a respected figure in football, aims to build the club's academy to compete in the Premier League and is hopeful of becoming the permanent manager. Despite speculation linking him with other clubs, Ramsey remains focused on QPR and believes he could be a top manager, crediting the 'Sport On Board' course for helping Les Ferdinand, the club's director of football, excel in his role.

The son of Brunei's Sultan, one of the world's wealthiest individuals, married 22-year-old Dayangku Raabi'atul 'Adawiyyah Pengiran Haji Bolkiah in a lavish ceremony held at the 1,788-room Istana Nural Iman palace in Bandar Seri Begawan, Brunei. The newlyweds, dressed in opulent traditional attire adorned with diamonds and other precious gems, were surrounded by nobility, foreign dignitaries, and representatives from other royal families. The wedding, which spans 11 days, showcases the immense wealth and cultural traditions of Brunei's royal family.

Matilda Kahl, an art director at Saatchi & Saatchi in New York, has worn the same outfit to work every day for three years as a way to eliminate the stress of choosing her clothes. Inspired by her male colleagues and a particularly stressful morning, she decided to simplify her wardrobe to a black trouser, white shirt, and a custom leather rosette. This uniform has not only reduced her financial spending and stress but has also given her a sense of control and confidence in her work environment.

A toddler named Ophelia Conant was nearly strangled when she became trapped in a gap of her cotbed, only being saved by her mother who saw the incident via a baby monitor. Phillip Dickens, the director of Baumhaus Ltd, a furniture supplier, was found guilty of placing an unsafe product on the market and was fined £50,000 with a suspended prison sentence. This incident, along with another involving a second toddler, highlighted the company's lack of proper quality control and adherence to British safety standards for the cotbeds manufactured in China and distributed in the UK.

Experts believe they have solved the mystery of how the Rapa Nui people placed distinctive red stone "hats" (pukao) on the heads of giant Moai statues on Easter Island, using basic physics and modeling techniques. Sean Hixon and his team concluded that the rounded shape of the pukao made it relatively easy to roll them up ramps to place them on the statues' heads, suggesting that fewer than ten men might have been needed to accomplish this task. This finding challenges previous theories that required more complex methods or larger numbers of people.

Shadow Chancellor Ed Balls indicated during a TV interview that Labour might consider raising the main rate of corporation tax to 26.5%, which would be higher than the current rate but still lower than other G7 countries, while also remaining evasive about potential changes to the 40p income tax rate. Critics argue that such proposals could jeopardize economic recovery and investment. Additionally, the Conservative Party announced plans to sell off up to £4 billion of Lloyds Bank shares to the public at a discount, aiming to recoup money for the government and encourage ownership among individual investors.

The Salt card is a credit card-sized device designed to eliminate the need for manually unlocking smartphones or tablets, automatically unlocking them when the user is nearby and locking them again when the user moves out of range. Created by Joel Paglione and Niko Zistakis, the Salt card connects to a user's phone via Bluetooth and can also alert the user if they leave their wallet behind. The inventors claim it saves users around 53 hours per year and is more secure than fingerprint scanners. The Salt card is currently available for pre-order online for $20 and is expected to be more secure than traditional password entry methods.

Middlesbrough secured a crucial victory against Wolves, thanks to goals from Jelle Vossen and Patrick Bamford, who also assisted the first goal. This win keeps Middlesbrough on track for automatic promotion to the Premier League. Patrick Bamford, on loan from Chelsea, has been in excellent form, scoring more goals in a single season than any other Boro player in the past 25 years, and shows potential for a first-team return to Chelsea.

The article highlights the largely unaddressed crimes of female Nazi guards at concentration camps, particularly at Auschwitz, who have mostly avoided prosecution due to their advanced age. Only three out of the 3,700 women who served in Nazi death camps have been investigated for their roles as accomplices to mass murder, and none have been tried in recent years. Despite efforts to locate and prosecute surviving SS guards, the passage of time and the physical condition of these former guards have hindered justice, leaving many victims and their families seeking accountability.

Alastair Cook and Jonathan Trott struggled once again at the crease during the first Test in Antigua, with both falling cheaply, leaving England struggling to establish a strong position. James Tredwell's impressive performance saw him pick up four wickets, contributing to West Indies' first-innings total of 295. Despite the setback, England managed a first-innings lead of 104, with Joe Root and Gary Ballance stabilizing the innings with an unbroken partnership.

In Israel, a company and university are unveiling technology that turns smartphones into tricorder-like devices, capable of analyzing the chemical composition of objects from a distance. This technology, which analyzes a material's "hyperspectral signature," or unique chemical fingerprint, has potential applications in various sectors including food, healthcare, and defense. The device works by capturing and processing information from across the electromagnetic spectrum, offering more detailed information than standard cameras.

Police are searching for 26-year-old Peter Fox, who is suspected of murdering his mother, Bernadette Fox, and his sister, Sarah Fox, in Merseyside. The bodies of Sarah and Bernadette were found half a mile apart; Sarah was reportedly stabbed multiple times, while Bernadette died from asphyxiation. Peter Fox was seen traveling to London on the night of the murders, and police are urging the public not to approach him.

The Boston Athletic Association is opening the Boston RunBase, a combination clubhouse, museum, and retail store, just a few blocks from the finish line of the Boston Marathon. This location, which opens in April, offers visitors the chance to learn about the marathon's history, run a replica course on a treadmill, and purchase running gear, all while supporting the local running community. The RunBase also serves as a year-round hub for the Boston Athletic Association, hosting events and connecting runners with resources and partners in the area.

Sarah Vine argues for a woman's right to present the car-focused television show "Top Gear," emphasizing her deep love for cars and her extensive experience with them. She highlights her diverse range of car ownership and her skills as a driver, including her ability to parallel park and avoid relying on modern convenience features. Vine suggests that the show is not just for male petrolheads and that women have just as much passion for cars and driving.

Research has shown that older fathers may increase the risk of various health issues in their offspring, including epilepsy, autism, breast cancer, and certain genetic disorders. As men age, the quality of their sperm declines, increasing the risk of DNA mutations and genetic defects in their children. While women are often advised about the risks of advanced maternal age, men should also be informed about potential risks associated with delayed fatherhood, such as higher chances of birth defects and genetic disorders in their children.

In March, a group of men gang-raped an unconscious 19-year-old woman on a beach in Panama City, Florida, while hundreds of spring break revelers watched and did nothing to intervene, as shown in a disturbing video released by the Bay County Sheriff’s Office. Two students from Alabama's Troy University, Delonte Martistee and Ryan Calhoun, were arrested for the sexual assault, but authorities are still searching for two additional suspects involved in the incident. Sheriff Frank McKeithen expressed outrage over the bystanders' indifference, describing the event as "the most disgusting, sickening thing" he had ever seen.

A mother named Kate Roberts successfully raised £2,000 in 24 hours to fund a special helmet for her son Miles, who was born with flat-head syndrome. The NHS does not cover such treatments, but the condition can lead to facial disfigurement and vision issues, prompting the mother to seek private treatment. After community support, Miles will begin wearing the custom-built helmet to correct the shape of his head.

A new review suggests that kicking, punching, and moving around during sleep, indicative of rapid eye movement sleep behavior disorder (RBD), may be an early sign of Parkinson's disease. Approximately half of individuals diagnosed with RBD develop Parkinson's or another neurological disorder within a decade, with up to 90% of people with RBD eventually developing a neurodegenerative condition. This finding could potentially serve as an early warning sign for Parkinson's, though not all cases of Parkinson's disease present with RBD initially.

Raheem Sterling's recent interview, where he indicated he was not ready to sign a new contract with Liverpool, was met with disappointment and frustration from many Liverpool fans, who view it as ungrateful given the club's support and investment in him. The club is considering letting him go if he insists on leaving, despite his potential value, and there is a sense among some fans that moving to Arsenal would be particularly unpopular. Sterling's performance has been inconsistent recently, and while he shows great promise, his current form and recent poor performance against Manchester United have fueled fan dissatisfaction.

Reigning Man of Steel Daryl Clark, who recently joined Warrington Wolves from Castleford Tigers, will return to face his former club in a Super League match on Easter Monday. Clark, despite leaving the Tigers, remains emotionally attached to the team and hopes they perform well. Warrington coach Tony Smith believes Clark deserves a positive reception from the visiting fans, highlighting the financial benefits his departure brought to the club.

David Moore, 25, attacked Rafal Cegielka, 45, during a school run incident in Burnley, Lancashire, after becoming enraged due to traffic congestion. Moore assaulted Cegielka, damaged his car with a stolen fencing panel, and later used a hockey stick to smash Cegielka’s vehicle while he was inside, causing £500 in damages. Moore pleaded guilty to several charges and received a suspended prison sentence, along with attending a violence intervention program and paying compensation.

Christian migrants from Africa, including Eritreans Haben and Samuel, have fled to escape beheadings by Islamic State fanatics in Libya. They faced the perilous journey across the Mediterranean, where many others have died, to seek safety in Europe. The Islamic State has established strongholds in Libya, using the chaos there to target and execute Christians, forcing many to deny their faith to survive.

Satellite images from Europe's Sentinel-1a revealed that Mount Everest shrunk by about one inch after the Nepal earthquake, while an area around Kathmandu uplifted by about 3.2 feet. These images, obtained through synthetic aperture radar interferometry, showed the detailed effects of the 7-magnitude earthquake, which killed thousands and affected millions. The satellite's ability to penetrate clouds and darkness allowed for unprecedented monitoring and support of relief efforts in the region.

Stanford professor Sebastian Thrun, who co-founded Google X, suggests that computers may soon be capable of transmitting complex human personalities, much like how data is currently transmitted. Thrun believes this technology is within reach and could potentially enable us to outsource our personal experiences and even our personalities into computers. However, virtual reality pioneer Jaron Lanier expressed skepticism about the ability to accurately capture and share personalities due to their fluid nature.

Following Freddie Gray's funeral, a small group of peace advocates attempted to maintain calm in Baltimore, but the situation escalated into widespread rioting and looting, overshadowing the initial calls for a peaceful demonstration. Despite efforts from clergy, family members, and community leaders to prevent violence, the unrest grew into an urban riot, with fires, looting, and clashes with police dominating the scene. The Gray family and their supporters emphasized that such violence was counterproductive and did not align with their quest for justice, though the rioting significantly marred their message.

A recent video has surfaced online featuring a group of fully veiled women practicing with machine guns and military drills in Syria, potentially linked to the Islamic State. The women, who appear to include British nationals among them, struggle with handling the heavy weapons and demonstrate basic training exercises while shouting pro-jihad slogans. The video was filmed at what was once a pilgrimage site, now used as a training ground for female extremists.

A 21-year-old morbidly obese woman named Rochelle Coulson receives £18,000 annually in benefits due to her sleep apnea, which she claims makes her a danger in the workplace. Despite doctors advising her to lose weight to improve her condition, Coulson requires a support worker to assist with meal planning and lacks the energy to work. Critics argue that the benefit system should not serve as a "comfort blanket" and that individuals should be encouraged to work rather than rely on benefits.

Bath faced a daunting prospect against Leinster in the first half, struggling with control and falling behind 15-5 at halftime due to poor performance and a controversial yellow card for Anthony Watson. However, Bath showed remarkable resilience and determination in the second half, thanks to the exceptional play of George Ford, ultimately coming within a penalty of winning the match. Despite falling just short, the team's spirit and improvement were praised, promising future success despite the narrow defeat.

A recent poll of key marginal seats showed a significant decline in support for UKIP, with the party losing ground in nine out of ten battleground constituencies, including Ukip leader Nigel Farage's own seat in Thanet South. This trend mirrors a broader national decline in UKIP support, with their share falling by over 25% in the past six months. Meanwhile, the Conservative Party is expected to retain control of five of the ten marginal seats it won in 2010, while Labour is poised to gain four seats, according to Lord Ashcroft’s poll.

David Crossley, a 63-year-old musculoskeletal therapist from Birmingham, developed large kidney stones due to his habit of neglecting hydration, particularly during busy workdays. Doctors attribute the rise in kidney stone cases to dehydration and changing dietary trends, such as low-carb, high-protein diets, which can increase the risk of stone formation. To prevent recurrence, patients are advised to maintain proper hydration, limit salt intake, and adhere to a balanced diet.

Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) chief Michele Leonhart is expected to resign due to allegations that DEA agents engaged in misconduct with prostitutes in Colombia, potentially compromising sensitive information. The White House declined to offer Leonhart a vote of confidence, and a U.S. congressional committee will investigate the claims. Leonhart testified that there was no evidence of sensitive information being leaked, but admitted it was "absolutely" possible that information had been compromised.

Researchers have discovered an enormous secondary magma chamber beneath Yellowstone National Park, which is much larger than previously thought and could fill the Grand Canyon 11 times over. This chamber, located 12 to 28 miles below the surface, contains mostly hot rock with only 2% molten rock that is too deep to directly cause an eruption. The discovery explains the high levels of carbon dioxide emissions from the supervolcano and provides insights into the structure of other supervolcanoes.

In August 2013, a 10-year-old boy named L.T. brutally murdered 6-year-old Lee Bonneau on a reservation in Saskatchewan, Canada, by beating him with a rock and a stick. Initially, L.T. claimed he had witnessed a stranger commit the murder but later confessed to being the actual perpetrator, pleading for his friends not to tell on him. Due to L.T.'s young age, he was not charged with the murder, and the case highlighted the need for better support and supervision for children with severe behavioral issues.

Chelsea Manning, a former U.S. Army private convicted of leaking classified documents to WikiLeaks and sentenced to 35 years in prison, has given her first in-depth interview from behind bars about her transition to a woman while serving her sentence. Despite facing numerous challenges, including restrictions on growing her hair and accessing certain amenities, Manning has been approved for hormone therapy and is using a telephone to maintain contact with supporters on social media. Reflecting on her journey, Manning discusses her difficult childhood, her experiences in the military, and the realization that she was a woman trapped in a male body, leading her to seek and eventually embrace her true identity.

Arsenal legend Ray Parlour believes Jack Wilshere has the potential to be a key player for the club, citing his talent and the recent success of Arsenal's young players. However, Parlour expresses concern over Wilshere's injury history, comparing him to Abou Diaby and questioning his ability to stay fit for a full season. Despite the concerns, Parlour remains optimistic about Arsenal's squad and believes, with the right signings, they could challenge for titles next season.

In Brisbane, a vigilante group called Wicked Pickets has begun spray-painting over offensive slogans on Wicked Campers' vans to combat what they perceive as violence against women, after the company failed to remove the slogans despite a petition of over 120,000 signatures. The slogans, which include derogatory comments about women and promote sexualized and violent imagery, have sparked outrage among local activists who argue that such language contributes to harmful attitudes towards women. In response, Wicked Campers' CEO has invited those offended to paint over the slogans, though the vigilantists argue this is insufficient given the persistence of the offensive content.

Tom Wood of Northampton Saints believes his team needs to regain their momentum after recent poor performances, particularly following the loss to Clermont in the Champions Cup. The Saints have been preparing intensively, including with 50 scrums, to address their current mini-slump ahead of a crucial match against Saracens. Meanwhile, Harlequins' winger Ugo Monye, who is retiring at the end of the season, is looking to finish strongly against Sale, while several other matches are previewed with predictions for outcomes.

A German man named Micha Stunz, who is 45 and lives in Berlin, has permanently enlarged his penis with silicone injections to a length of 9 inches and a weight of up to 9.5 pounds, significantly altering his life in both positive and negative ways. Stunz underwent the procedure not for aesthetic reasons but to feel "better," despite the difficulties it has caused in his sex life. Despite the challenges, he sees the enlargement as a form of self-expression and has become more creative in the bedroom as a result.

Kezzia French, the mother of Andrea Fowler, who was killed by her father in 1999, is holding a second funeral for her daughter due to discovering that Andrea's vital organs were retained without her consent. The revelation came after a national police audit in 2010, and further information about the disposal of Andrea's brain in 2009 was disclosed to Ms. French in 2012. Ms. French feels lied to and coned by the authorities and is planning to make formal complaints to the relevant hospitals and trusts involved.

Two best friends, Jamie Jewitt and Henry Rogers, transformed their lives through significant weight loss and modeling careers, proving that determination and self-belief can lead to achieving one's dreams. Starting from self-conscious teens, they both lost substantial weight through rigorous diets and training, eventually becoming sought-after models for major brands like Tom Ford, Armani, and Prada. Now using their success, they aim to address and reduce the stigma around male body image and insecurities, hoping to encourage more open conversations about these issues.

The Mail on Sunday revealed that Qatar spent an astonishing £17.2 billion on deals and lobbying efforts to secure the 2022 World Cup bid, which it won 14-8 against the USA in a FIFA executive committee vote. This spending included legitimate trade deals and cash payments from secret slush funds managed by Qatar’s executive committee member, Mohammed bin Hammam, to various football officials. In response to these revelations, there is growing calls for FIFA to reconsider its decision to award the tournament to Qatar.

Shaker Aamer, Britain's last Guantanamo Bay detainee, is expected to be released as early as June, according to US government sources. Aamer, who has been held without charge or trial for over 13 years, is likely to be one of eleven prisoners transferred from the notorious facility within weeks. This development comes after Aamer was previously cleared for release by both the Bush and Obama administrations, and follows pressure from the UK government and international human rights organizations.

Jo Gilchrist, a 27-year-old mother, contracted a severe staph infection from using her best friend's makeup brush, which led to her being confined to a wheelchair for the rest of her life. The infection, a form of community-associated MRSA, damaged her spine severely, leaving her with no feeling below her belly button and losing control over her bowel and bladder. Despite the grim prognosis, Jo is fighting back and is gradually regaining some mobility, thanks to ongoing treatment and support from her friends who have rallied around her, including a musician who expressed solidarity through social media.

Simon Mitchell, a terminally ill fundraiser, stole a laptop, sat nav, and phone from Donna's Dream House, a charity for terminally ill children in Blackpool, after initially gaining the charity's trust with promises of celebrity contacts to raise its profile. Mitchell, who claimed to be completing a "bucket list" of good deeds before his own terminal illness, admitted to the thefts during a three-year investigation and pleaded guilty at Preston Crown Court. The charity chairman expressed disappointment in Mitchell's betrayal and emphasized the importance of due diligence when accepting offers of support, especially during vulnerable times.

Perth couple Sharon and Nick Chalwell, who have been trying to conceive for over seven years through various fertility treatments, found an egg donor through a radio station call-out, connecting them with Shannon Mann, a 22-year-old who has already donated once and wishes to help others. Before proceeding, the trio must undergo extensive counseling to ensure informed consent and address ethical considerations. Their story aims to raise awareness about egg donation and address the shortage of donors in Australia.

Ten years after becoming the Duchess of Cornwall, Camilla Parker-Bowles has transformed from being Britain's most hated woman to a beloved member of the royal family, with 50% of Britons loving her and 56% crediting her with boosting Charles' popularity. Her success is attributed to her charm, down-to-earth nature, and dedication to charitable causes, particularly her long-standing support of the National Osteoporosis Society. Camilla's relationship with the royal family, especially her growing bond with the Queen and the Prince of Wales, has also contributed to her newfound acceptance and happiness within the royal household.

Belle Gibson, the founder of The Whole Pantry app, admitted in a recent interview that she fabricated her terminal brain cancer diagnosis, prompting a psychological analysis suggesting she may suffer from a combination of narcissistic personality disorder and antisocial personality disorder. Leading psychologist Jo Lamble pointed out common traits such as deception, lack of remorse, and charisma, which Gibson displayed, indicating a need for attention and admiration possibly stemming from a history of neglect. Experts believe that social media platforms may have contributed to and exacerbated her behavior, potentially influencing others to idolize her false narrative.

The Liberal Democrats are facing a significant electoral challenge, potentially losing at least 20 MPs and possibly being reduced to "the thirties" in terms of representation, according to senior party sources. Despite this, Nick Clegg is maintaining a targeted campaign strategy, focusing on about 60 key marginal seats, emphasizing their potential to form a coalition government should they secure a seat count in the 30s. Meanwhile, opinion polls suggest a tight race, with the Conservatives leading slightly but the outcome remaining uncertain.

A diverse group of 24 individuals, including a union plumber, school teacher, and survivor of the 1999 Columbine High School massacre, have been chosen to serve as jurors in the highly publicized death penalty trial of James Holmes, the Colorado theater shooter. The lengthy and intricate jury selection process, which began in January and concluded on Tuesday, involved questioning hundreds of potential jurors and was deemed one of the most extensive in U.S. history. The jurors will determine whether Holmes should be executed or receive a life sentence without parole, based on their assessment of his mental state at the time of the shooting.

Researchers have discovered that the bombardier beetle mimics a machine gun by mixing chemicals in an internal 'reaction chamber' in its abdomen, which it then fires as a boiling hot spray when threatened. This behavior involves combining chemicals to create an explosive mixture that heats and propels the defensive load, allowing the beetle to aim precisely and deliver a powerful spray. The study reveals that the beetle's spray pulsation is caused by the temporary displacement of a thin cuticle region near the mixing valve, creating a passive closure mechanism that generates the pulsed delivery, a phenomenon not previously understood.

Researchers have discovered a striking similarity in the distribution patterns of skin cells and desert "fairy circles" in Namibia, despite their apparent unrelatedness. Both exhibit a hexagonal arrangement with most units having six neighbors, a pattern previously observed in skin cells and now found in these enigmatic desert formations. This unexpected similarity suggests underlying mechanisms that could be universal across vastly different scales in nature.

German rapper-turned-ISIS terrorist Denis Cuspert, known as "Abu Talha al-Amani," has released a propaganda video calling on sleeper cells in Europe to carry out attacks, including in Britain, Germany, and France. The video, which includes horrific footage and calls for jihad, follows heightened security measures in the UK for World War I commemorative events. Intelligence suggests that the number of Britons joining ISIS may be around 1,600, with at least five people leaving the UK for Syria and Iraq weekly.

A 19-month-old girl named Rosannah Gundry was diagnosed with stage three neuroblastoma, a form of cancer, after a tumour the size of a football and weighing over seven kilograms was found around her organs and pressing against her spine. Despite undergoing chemotherapy, the treatment-resistant tumour developed a protective barrier making it immune to the medication, leaving the family searching for specialized treatment options abroad. Rosannah's aunt is raising funds and seeking medical advice from specialists in the United States to provide her with a better chance at life.

A devastating avalanche hit Everest Base Camp following a powerful earthquake in Nepal, causing at least 17 fatalities and leaving dozens injured or missing. Climbers and local workers faced life-threatening conditions as the ground shook and snow descended upon them, forcing them to seek shelter in their tents. Rescue efforts were complicated by aftershocks and impassable terrain, with helicopters assisting in the evacuation of stranded climbers.

Jack Wilshere has taken a significant step towards recovery from his ankle injury by playing 90 minutes for Arsenal's under-21 side in a 4-1 victory over Stoke City. His performance suggests he may return to the senior team before the end of the season, though he exerted only a quiet influence compared to the hat-trick hero Alex Iwobi. Additionally, Mikel Arteta and Abou Diaby also participated in the match while still recovering from their respective injuries.

Neil Moore, a conman and fraudster, escaped from Wandsworth Prison by sending a fake email to the prison authorities posing as a court clerk, and was subsequently sentenced to seven years in jail. Moore had been remanded in custody for a £1.8 million fraud and had also set up a fraudulent website while in prison. His escape was motivated by his fear of being harmed by fellow inmates after forming a relationship with a transgender individual.

Doctors and nutritionists are cautioning against the trend of completely cutting out carbohydrate-rich foods, particularly healthier wholegrains, from one's diet. While some processed carbohydrates like white bread can contribute to weight gain and health issues, experts recommend choosing healthier options and maintaining a balanced intake. Nutritionist Susie Burrell highlights that different types of bread vary significantly in nutritional value, with wholegrain and lower-carb options being more beneficial than highly processed ones.

The early stages of the U.S. presidential campaign have seen several notable mistakes from potential candidates, including New Jersey Governor Chris Christie calling for cuts to Social Security and opposing marijuana legalization, which could harm his moderate image; Senator Ted Cruz enrolling in the Affordable Care Act despite his opposition, raising questions about his authenticity; and Senator Rand Paul's aggressive behavior in interviews, which highlighted his temperament and interactions with women. Meanwhile, Hillary Clinton's campaign has managed to avoid major gaffes but faced a minor issue regarding her family's immigration history. These early missteps could shape voter perceptions, though the overall impact on the campaign remains to be seen.

Toulon faced a challenging match against Clermont Auvergne at Stade Velodrome, narrowly securing a victory through a controversial try in extra-time after being reduced to 14 men. The match, part of the inaugural Champions Cup, highlighted the difficulties in executing a cohesive game due to poor handling and numerous turnovers. Despite Toulon's win, the performance did not live up to expectations, with both teams struggling to maintain fluency and rhythm. The final between these two French giants in the upcoming Champions Cup is anticipated to be a fierce and historic confrontation, potentially marking Toulon's attempt at a hat-trick of European titles against their rivals from Clermont.

Celebrity chef Matt Kemp, known for his anger management issues, was seen verbally abusing his pregnant wife on national television during an episode of SBS’s Heat in the Kitchen in 2004. Reflecting on his past behavior, Kemp now regrets his actions and credits his desire to be a better father as the catalyst for changing his attitude and behavior. Kemp and his ex-wife have since separated, and he is currently working at Charing Cross Hotel in Sydney.

US researchers have identified a gene called TcSAD1 that controls the melting point of cocoa butter, potentially leading to the creation of new types of chocolate, cosmetics, and pharmaceuticals. This discovery could also help in developing climate-resistant cocoa plants, boosting yields and supporting farmers' incomes. The finding is significant given the current global cocoa shortfall, which could reach a million tonnes by 2020 due to rising demand and production challenges.

In January 2014, Mikaeel Kular, a three-year-old toddler, was killed by his mother, Rosdeep Adekoya, in Fife, Scotland. Despite multiple visits from social and health service workers over the preceding months, a review found that the circumstances leading to his death could not have been predicted. The report identified areas for improvement and made recommendations for future action, acknowledging the challenges faced by professionals during organizational changes and heavy caseloads.

Victoria Wasteney, a devout Christian, was given a written warning for praying for a Muslim colleague and inviting her to church events, leading to an employment tribunal that found she had bullied her colleague. Wasteney is now challenging the decision, arguing that her freedom of conscience and religion were violated, and that this case highlights the increasing difficulties faced by religious individuals in the workplace. She believes the case has broader implications for protecting religious expression in the workplace.

Chelsea secured a vital 1-0 victory over Manchester United at Stamford Bridge, taking a significant step towards the Premier League title with Eden Hazard scoring the only goal in the 38th minute. Jose Mourinho's team showcased strong defensive organization, with key players like Cesar Azpilicueta, John Terry, and Nemanja Matic performing well. Manchester United struggled to break through, with Wayne Rooney's attacking influence notably blunted by his midfield role, while Chelsea's Eden Hazard was rated the standout player of the match.

Three men in their 50s from the York area have been arrested on suspicion of murdering missing chef Claudia Lawrence, who was last seen in 2009. The arrests are part of a renewed investigation into her disappearance, which has included searches of several houses near her home and a fresh review of evidence. The case remains unsolved, with the body of Claudia Lawrence yet to be found.

A 92-year-old pensioner, Pamela Clothier, found her home cleared out and possessions removed without her consent after being hospitalized, leaving her devastated and critical of both her family and the charity involved. The charity, Age UK, had acted on her son’s instructions to clear the house, believing she intended to sell it, despite her objections. Mrs. Clothier is calling for changes in the law to prevent such actions without explicit permission from the homeowner.

In July 2013, a fire at Paul's Hair World in Manchester's Northern Quarter resulted in the death of firefighter Stephen Hunt, 38, while he and a colleague were battling the flames. A 16-year-old girl, who initially faced charges of arson after discarding a cigarette that caused the fire, was cleared of the charge and instead found to be "guilty only of being careless" by a judge. The case, which involved complex scientific analysis, ultimately concluded that the fire could have been accidentally started by the discarded cigarette.

Sofia Vergara is involved in a legal dispute with her ex-husband Nick Loeb over frozen embryos they created in 2013. Vergara's lawyer maintains that she has no intention of destroying the embryos but also has no plans to use them, stating that she has moved on from the idea of having children with Loeb. The case highlights the complexities of surrogacy agreements and the challenges faced when relationships end after creating embryos for potential use.

In response to widespread protests from Japanese-American groups and the actor George Takei, an East Coast auction house has canceled the sale of 450 photos and artifacts from World War II internment camps. The items, collected by the renowned craftsman Allen Eaton, included photos and crafts made by internees and were intended to tell the story of the incarceration of Japanese Americans. The cancellation came after the Heart Mountain Wyoming Foundation threatened legal action, highlighting the sensitive nature of selling such historically significant items.

Australian bride-to-be Stephanie Scott, 26, vanished on Easter Sunday while preparing for her wedding, leaving her fiancé and family devastated. Despite not finding her body, police charged a 24-year-old man with her murder, forcing her loved ones to plan her funeral instead of her wedding. Family and friends, including Scott's sister who flew in from abroad, have joined in the search efforts and are facing the heartbreak of mourning rather than celebrating.

The article discusses a new series called "Chaos Caught on Camera," which premieres on the Science Channel on April 13, 2015.
